Burkina Faso : Le gouvernement annonce la fin du rapatriement des orpailleurs expulsés de Guinée
items.description: Dans un communiqué publié ce vendredi 20 novembre 2026 et signé par le porte-parole de l'exécutif, le Service d'information du gouvernement (SIG) annonce la fin des opérations de rapatriement des orpailleurs burkinabè expulsés de Guinée. Les autorités burkinabè précisent qu' à la date du 18 novembre 2026, 76 169 personnes, dont 74 452 hommes et 1 717 femmes, ont été rapatriées. Parmi elles figurent 15 968 enfants. Engagées le 2 novembre 2026, ces opérations ont concerné plusieurs milliers de ressortissants burkinabè. Des citoyens d'autres nationalités ont également été concernés par ces mesures et ont bénéficié de l'accueil et de l'hospitalité spontanés des autorités et du peuple maliens, rappelle le gouvernement dans le communiqué. items.title: World Toilet Day 2026: WaterAid Ghana calls for increased sanitation investment, urges districts to emulate Bongo
items.description: WaterAid Ghana has called for sustained investment in sanitation infrastructure, stronger local government leadership and greater accountability to ensure that every Ghanaian has access to safe and decent toilet facilities. The water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH)-focused organisation says access to decent toilets must be treated as an essential public service rather than a privilege, stressing that inadequate sanitation continues to threaten public health, human dignity and equality, particularly among women, girls and vulnerable populations. Speaking at the 2026 World Toilet Day celebration held in Bongo in the Upper East Region, the Country Director of WaterAid Ghana, Ewurabena Yanyi-Akofur, said millions of people continued to live without access to decent toilet facilities, exposing them to preventable health risks and undermining their quality of life. “This is not merely an infrastructure gap. It is a public health concern, a question of dignity, and an issue of equality,” she stated. She highlighted the difficulties faced by schoolgirls who miss classes because of inadequate toilet facilities, pregnant women without access to appropriate sanitation, and persons with disabilities who struggle to use inaccessible facilities. According to her, these challenges have far-reaching consequences for education, maternal health, social inclusion and the overall well-being of communities. “These are not abstract development challenges. These are real experiences that affect people’s ability to live healthy, productive and dignified lives,” she said. The WaterAid Ghana Country Director commended the leaders and people of Bongo for their commitment to improving sanitation, citing the Bongo Sanitation Challenge as an example of how local ownership can help address sanitation problems. WaterAid’s partnership with the Bongo Traditional Authority, led by the Chief, Naba Baba Salifu Lemyaarum, and the District Health Directorate has led to the construction of household latrines and the declaration of Open Defecation Free (ODF) status in several communities in the district. She said the initiative demonstrated the importance of community participation and leadership in promoting improved sanitation practices and tackling open defecation. Ms Yanyi-Akofur urged stakeholders to build on the momentum generated by the initiative to ensure that commitments translate into improved sanitation facilities and healthier households. “Let Bongo be an example of what is possible when a community makes sanitation everyone’s business. And let the commitment we make here today inspire action across every district in Ghana,” she said. She reaffirmed WaterAid Ghana’s commitment to working with government institutions, traditional authorities, communities and development partners to advance universal access to clean water, decent toilets and good hygiene. The Deputy Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Rita Naa Odoley Sowah, commended WaterAid Ghana for its support towards improving sanitation and promoting partnerships to eliminate open defecation. Addressing the gathering, she said achieving Sustainable Development Goal 17, which emphasises partnerships, required collaboration among government institutions, development partners, traditional authorities and communities. The Deputy Minister said the government was prioritising sanitation financing through the District Assemblies Common Fund (DACF), citing the allocation of 10 per cent of the fund to Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies (MMDAs) for sanitation-related activities. “Through the DACF, we have the financial support; the 10 percent of the Common Fund to the MMDAs geared towards sanitation.” She explained that the investments would support waste treatment facilities, liquid waste management infrastructure, sanitation equipment, policy development, public education and behavioural change. She said: “And then investment in sanitation infrastructure, investing in waste treatment facilities, liquid waste management infrastructure, and then supplying sanitation equipment, development of policies and regulatory framework, public education and behavioural change. These are all geared towards ending open defecation.” The Upper East Regional Minister, Donatus Akamugri, called for renewed commitment from all 15 Municipal and District Assemblies in the region to improve household and public toilet facilities and eliminate open defecation. He said poor sanitation continued to expose communities to preventable diseases, contaminate water sources and undermine public health, with women, children and persons with disabilities among the most affected. “For the Upper East Region, this calls for a renewed commitment from all the 15 Municipal and District Assemblies to improve household and public toilet facilities, eradicate open defecation, strengthen sanitation management and promote responsible hygiene practices,” he stated. Mr Akamugri urged local authorities to move beyond occasional sanitation exercises and adopt sustainable approaches that encourage continuous community participation and responsibility. “Sanitation must move beyond occasional cleanup exercises to become a sustained public responsibility and a way of life,” he added. The World Toilet Day celebration in Bongo, held under the theme “ From Open Defecation to Open Opportunity Through the Gender Lens ,” provided an opportunity for stakeholders to assess progress and renew commitments towards achieving universal access to decent sanitation. The event also highlighted the role of WaterAid Ghana in supporting local leadership, community participation and partnerships to improve water, sanitation and hygiene services in Bongo and the wider Upper East Region. For WaterAid Ghana, achieving universal access to sanitation requires sustained investment, effective partnerships, strong local leadership and deliberate efforts to ensure that vulnerable populations are not excluded. The organisation reiterated that access to safe toilets should never depend on a person’s income, age, disability or geographical location. “Everyone deserves a decent toilet. No one should be left behind,” the WaterAid Ghana Country Director concluded.

items.title: Touré Kunda fait résonner la musique sénégalaise dans le monde du jeu vidéo
items.description: Le groupe Touré Kunda figure dans la programmation musicale de Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6), le nouvel opus de la célèbre franchise de Rockstar Games. Son titre « Nobel » a été retenu pour la station de radio virtuelle Kaleidoscope FM. Une nouvelle vitrine internationale pour notre patrimoine musical , dans une saga vidéoludique qui a traversé près de trois décennies. La musique sénégalaise s'invite dans l'un des univers vidéoludiques les plus populaires au monde. Le groupe Touré Kunda fait partie des artistes sélectionnés pour accompagner les joueurs de Grand Theft Auto VI. L'information figure dans les crédits musicaux officiels publiés par Rockstar Games sur son site internet. Le morceau « Nobel » apparaît dans la programmation de Kaleidoscope FM, une station de radio virtuelle animée par le personnage de DJ Dicky, interprété par l'acteur britannique Jeremy Irons. Cette présence prend une dimension particulière au regard de l'histoire de la franchise. Lancée en 1997, la saga Grand Theft Auto, communément appelée GTA, a progressivement évolué pour devenir une référence mondiale du jeu vidéo. À ses débuts, le premier opus, développé par le studio écossais DMA Design, proposait une expérience en deux dimensions, avec une vue de dessus et un univers ouvert dans lequel les joueurs incarnaient des personnages évoluant dans des villes fictives. Un premier tournant intervient en 2001 avec GTA III. Le passage à la 3D transforme profondément l'expérience de jeu et ouvre une nouvelle ère pour la franchise. Suivent GTA Vice City en 2002, qui plonge les joueurs dans une ville inspirée du Miami des années 1980, puis GTA San Andreas en 2004, dont l'univers s'inspire notamment de la Californie du début des années 1990. Treize années d'attente En 2008, GTA IV marque une nouvelle étape avec une narration plus approfondie et un univers urbain renouvelé. Cinq ans plus tard, GTA V rencontre un succès commercial considérable. Sorti en 2013, cet opus se distingue notamment par la possibilité d'incarner trois protagonistes et par le développement de GTA Online, son mode multijoueur qui prolonge l'expérience au-delà de la campagne principale. Après treize années d'attente depuis le précédent épisode numéroté, GTA VI poursuit cette histoire en ramenant les joueurs à Vice City, dans l'État fictif de Leonida, inspiré de la Floride. La musique y conserve une place importante. Les stations de radio virtuelles permettent de naviguer entre plusieurs genres et univers musicaux, faisant de la bande-son une composante essentielle de l'identité du jeu. C'est dans cet environnement que s'inscrit la présence de Touré Kunda. Fondé par les frères Ismaïla et Sixu Touré, le groupe s'est imposé comme l'une des formations emblématiques de la musique sénégalaise et africaine. Son parcours international et son répertoire, nourri de sonorités traditionnelles et d'influences diverses, ont contribué à faire connaître la richesse musicale du continent bien au-delà de ses frontières. La disparition d'Ismaïla Touré, survenue en décembre 2023, n'a toutefois pas effacé l’empreinte laissée par cette formation. À travers son répertoire et son héritage musical, Touré Kunda continue de marquer les esprits et de traverser les générations. La présence de son titre « Nobel » dans GTA 6 en constitue une nouvelle illustration. A.N

items.title: Transmission lines restored after grid disturbance – NISO
items.description: The Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) says it has restored all transmission lines that tripped during a grid disturbance on Friday. The management of NISO said this in a statement in Abuja on Friday. The ​‌‍‌​⁠‍⁠⁠‍‍⁠​⁠​​‌‍‌​system operator also said that the incident was not a system collapse. It said that the disturbance resulted from the tripping of some transmission line, which caused load losses in parts of the country. ”NISO wishes to clarify that the grid disturbance experienced earlier today was not a system collapse. “It resulted from the tripping of some transmission lines, which caused load losses in parts of the country. ”At 12:34 p.m., the Omotosho–Ikeja West transmission line tripped, resulting in a significant load drop within the Lagos Complex. ”Subsequently, at 12:50 p.m, the Ihovbor–Oshogbo transmission line tripped alongside the Benin–Egbin and Ihovbor–Ajaokuta transmission lines, resulting in load losses in some parts of the country,” it said. The system operator said that prompt emergency response measures were activated by the relevant operational teams in coordination with TCN to stabilize the grid and restore affected transmission lines. It said that all the affected lines had since been successfully restored to normal operation as of 2:49 p.m. on Friday. It reaffirmed its commitment to maintaining grid stability, coordinating system operations, and ensuring the reliable and secure operation of the Nigerian electricity grid. ”The public is advised to rely on official communications from NISO for accurate information on developments within the national electricity grid,” it said. (NAN) The post Transmission lines restored after grid disturbance – NISO appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Afenifere demands prosecution of sponsors of campaign violence
items.description: …Raises alarm over rising attacks ahead of 2027 elections By Adeola Badru The pan-Yoruba socio-political organisation, Afenifere, has raised the alarm over increasing political violence ahead of the 2027 general elections, calling for the arrest and prosecution of perpetrators and their sponsors. The organisation warned that the growing incidents of thuggery, intimidation and inflammatory political rhetoric posed a serious threat to the country’s democratic process. Afenifere, in a statement issued on Friday by its National Publicity Secretary, Jare Ajayi, called on political parties, candidates, their sponsors and supporters to end violence and ensure that campaigns were conducted in accordance with the Constitution and the Electoral Act. Ajayi expressed concern over reported attacks on political figures, campaign convoys and supporters in different parts of the country, warning that the growing atmosphere of hostility could undermine public confidence in the electoral process and endanger lives. Among the incidents cited was the reported attack on the motorcade of President Bola Tinubu on Friday, November 13, shortly after he observed Jumu’ah prayers at the Central Mosque, Abuja. According to the organisation, assailants threw stones and other dangerous objects at the departing presidential convoy, damaging several vehicles and injuring some security operatives. Afenifere also condemned the attack on supporters of the Accord Party governorship candidate in Oyo State, Oriyomi Hamzat, around the Molete area of Ibadan, which reportedly resulted in the death of a 40-year-old supporter, Azeez Tajudeen. It described the incident as particularly disturbing, saying the destruction of vehicles and loss of life highlighted the consequences of allowing political differences to degenerate into violence. The organisation further listed the reported attack on the convoy of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) vice-presidential candidate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, in Bichi, Kano State; the reported assault on the convoy of the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, in Calabar, Cross River State; and disruptions of political gatherings, particularly those of the APC and ADC in Sokoto, Kebbi and Lagos states. It said the incidents reflected a disturbing pattern requiring urgent intervention by political leaders and security agencies. Ajayi also recalled the warning by former President Goodluck Jonathan at the 2026 Goodluck Jonathan Foundation Peace Conference in Abuja, where he cautioned political leaders against running their parties like rival cult groups. Jonathan had warned against recruiting and exploiting young Nigerians for political violence, saying such practices could plunge the country into avoidable crises. Similarly, Senate President Godswill Akpabio had cautioned youths against allowing themselves to be used for political violence, warning that perpetrators could face serious criminal charges, including treasonable felony. Afenifere also referenced concerns raised by former Head of State, General Abdulsalami Abubakar, and the National Peace Committee’s Co-convener, Most Rev. Matthew Kukah, over inflammatory political campaigns. The interventions, it noted, followed reports of about 60 election-related incidents across the country within a month. The organisation also recalled President Tinubu’s directive condemning political violence across party lines and insisting that the 2027 elections should be defined by ideas rather than hostility. Highlighting the legal implications of electoral violence, Afenifere reminded political parties, candidates and their sponsors that recruiting, organising or financing political thugs constituted a criminal offence under Nigerian law. It cited Section 227 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which prohibits political parties and associations from retaining, organising, training or equipping individuals or groups to use physical force or coercion in promoting political objectives. It also referenced Section 78 of the Electoral Act, which, according to the organisation, prescribes fines of N5 million for a first offence and N7 million for subsequent offences by political parties, as well as N500,000 for every day the offence continues. Individuals or groups who aid or abet such violations could also face a fine of N5 million, imprisonment for five years or both, it said. Ajayi further cited Sections 92 and 93 of the Electoral Act, which criminalise political thuggery and the direct or indirect use or threat of force during election campaigns. He said offenders could face up to 12 months’ imprisonment or a fine of N1 million, while political parties found culpable could also incur financial penalties. “The provisions of the laws are quite clear. But impunity persists because sponsors of violence are rarely brought to book,” Ajayi said. He urged political leaders to call their supporters to order, stressing that those seeking political offices had a responsibility to ensure peaceful campaigns. The Afenifere spokesman also appealed to Nigerian youths not to allow themselves to be used as instruments of violence by politicians. “Nigerian youths must refuse to be used as cannon fodders by desperate politicians whose own children are safely tucked away from harm,” he warned. He urged political actors to respect the President’s position that the 2027 elections should be a democratic contest characterised by the exchange of ideas, peaceful participation and respect for the rights of Nigerians. Afenifere further called on stakeholders to ensure that political parties and candidates enjoyed equal protection and freedom to campaign in every part of the country without harassment, intimidation or threats to their safety. The organisation specifically challenged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), the Nigeria Police Force and the judiciary to move beyond public condemnations and take concrete action against electoral violence. It demanded the prompt arrest and prosecution of those responsible for attacks, including individuals and groups financing or sponsoring them, as well as the disqualification of offenders where permitted by law. Afenifere insisted that accountability should not end with the arrest of foot soldiers, but must extend to those who finance, organise and deploy political thugs. It warned that failure to decisively address political violence could undermine the credibility of the 2027 elections and threaten Nigeria’s democratic stability beyond the polls. The post Afenifere demands prosecution of sponsors of campaign violence appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Lagos diverts traffic in Ikeja for Saturday’s race
items.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Government has announced intermittent traffic diversions along major roads in Ikeja ahead of the third edition of the Capital City Race scheduled for Saturday, November 21, 2026. The traffic management arrangement, according to the Commissioner for Transportation, Oluwaseun Osiyemi, will commence at 7 a.m. to ensure the smooth conduct of the 10-kilometre race. Roads and corridors to be affected include Ikeja City Mall, Billings Way, Kudirat Abiola Way, Opebi Link Bridge, Adeniyi Jones, Oba Akran Road by the Lagos State University Teaching Hospital (LASUTH), and Archbishop Vining Memorial Church. Osiyemi said personnel of the Lagos State Traffic Management Authority (LASTMA), Nigeria Police Force (NPF), Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) and Lagos State Neighbourhood Safety Corps (LNSC) would be deployed to junctions and intersections along the race route to manage traffic. He explained that the diversions would be partial, with affected roads reopened intermittently to motorists as runners cleared each section of the route. The commissioner, however, did not specify when the traffic restrictions would end and normal vehicular movement fully resume. The state government appealed to motorists to cooperate with traffic management officials and exercise patience throughout the event to minimise inconvenience. The post Lagos diverts traffic in Ikeja for Saturday’s race appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: « Nour. Noureddine Melikechi » : le récit intime du physicien algérien de la NASA
items.description: Un enfant de Thenia à 50 km à l’est d’Alger qui intègre la NASA, cela ne court pas les rues. Écrit par Rym Khelil, « Nour. Noureddine Melikechi » (éditions barzakh) retrace le parcours extraordinaire de Noureddine Melikechi. Chercheur en physique atomique, moléculaire et optique, le professeur est membre de l’équipe scientifique des deux plus grandes missions de la NASA visant l’exploration de Mars. Par ailleurs, il est pionnier d’une nouvelle technique d’analyse qui permet le dépistage précoce du cancer de l’ovaire, désormais utilisée pour d’autres types de cancer. Noureddine Melikechi raconte son itinéraire et dévoile sa vision de la vie Aujourd’hui, Noureddine Melikechi est professeur de physique et doyen du Kennedy College of Sciences à l’université de Massachusetts Lowell. « Ce livre décrit mon itinéraire et ma perception des expériences que j’ai vécues » écrit-il dans l’avant-propos de ce récit autobiographique dont il a confié l’écriture à Rym Khelil. Enfance, études, voyages, recherches… tout est raconté à la voix narrative. Noureddine Melikechi est né en 1958 à Thenia, commune de la wilaya de Boumerdès. Le chercheur évoque la relation fusionnelle qu’il entretenait avec sa sœur Hassiba, docteur en microbiologie de l’eau. Décédée en 2016 des suites d’un cancer, il lui rend hommage : « À chaque fois que je la quittais pour retourner aux États-Unis, je vivais un déchirement (…) depuis, je sais qu’il faut vivre. Vivre ses passions, ses relations, faire ce que l’on veut, faire tant que l’on peut le faire. Le faire. Ne pas attendre ». Après le collège, Noureddine est interne au lycée Abane Ramdane d’El Harrach. Au début, il pense s’orienter vers la médecine mais ses professeurs lui conseillent les mathématiques, matière où il excelle. En 1976, le bachelier entre à l’université de Bab Ezzouar. Il évoque les contraintes dues au manque de transport reliant sa ville natale au pôle universitaire. « Je n’oublierai jamais le jour où j’arrivai très en retard à un examen à cause du fameux train insolent qui ne s’arrêtait qu’à Oued Smar. J’avais marché dans les marécages, pataugé dans la boue avant d’arriver en salle d’examen ». Le choc du décès du président Boumediene Il cite également comment lui et ses camarades ont appris, en plein cours, le décès du président Houari Boumediène le 27 décembre 1978. Une onde d’inquiétude avait alors parcouru les amphithéâtres de l’université. « Quelle direction allait prendre le pouvoir ? (…). Dans les mois qui suivirent, nous assistâmes à la naissance d’associations politiques, ainsi qu’à l’émergence de ‘nouveaux’ courants politiques : islamiste, communiste, démocrate … », raconte le physicien. En 1980, l’étudiant quitte l’Algérie pour poursuivre son doctorat au Royaume Uni. Une grande amitié le lie alors à la poignée d’Algériens qui fréquente la même université. « C’est ensemble qu’en juin 1982, dans une ambiance euphorique, nous suivîmes l’historique Allemagne-Algérie, où les Fennecs jouant pour la première fois de leur histoire en Coupe du monde vainquirent les champions d’Europe de l’époque, largement favorables », relate-t-il. Professeur Melikechi se confie sur l’entrée dans sa vie de celle qui deviendra son épouse et la mère de ses deux enfants : Omar et Lilia. Anne était étudiante en économie. Le couple se rencontre pour la première fois dans le réfectoire de l’université. En 1989, les deux étudiants célèbrent leur mariage à Thenia. Noureddine Melikechi raconte pourquoi il a quitté la France Après un bref passage par Toulouse en 1996, le couple quitte la France pour s’installer aux USA. « Je rejoignis Toulouse à l’été 1996 où j’ai appris beaucoup en travaillant avec une équipe de recherche toulousaine. Le sujet était passionnant, les chercheurs très sympathiques, le matériel à l’avant-garde du progrès et la région toulousaine très belle, mais l’atmosphère en France ne me rassurait pas », confie le professeur. L’environnement social dans lequel il projetait d’élever ses enfants le rebutait. Lors de l’élection présidentielle française de 1995, Jean-Marie Le Pen, fondateur du Front national (aujourd’hui Rassemblement national), avait fait une percée notable. « Cela me rebuta. La poussée de la propagande nationaliste et raciste, les affiches dans la rue, la banalisation de la haine de l’autre, tout cela nous fit remettre en question, ma femme et moi, nos projets d’installation en France », relate Noureddine Melikechi. « À l’université du Delaware, j’eu la chance de rencontrer des personnes extrêmement intéressantes et inspirantes qui influencèrent profondément ma carrière. C’est là qu’il approfondit ses recherches dans la spectroscopie laser et créa OSCAR (Optical Science Center for Applied Research) », explique le Professeur dont le nom sera porté jusqu’à l’éternité par un programme de recherche à l’université du Massachusetts aux États-Unis. Le parcours flamboyant d’un homme parti de rien Même à l’autre bout du monde, le chercheur reste très proche de l’Algérie. Il évoque l’inquiétude et l’angoisse qui le rongèrent suite au séisme de Boumerdès en 2003. À l'affût de la moindre information sur sa famille qui vivait non loin de l’épicentre du tremblement de terre, il tomba par hasard sur un journal télévisé où son père, interviewé par une chaîne française décrivait la situation catastrophique vécue par les habitants de Thenia suite à ce drame. Un parcours flamboyant d’un homme parti de rien et qui a cru en lui, en la force du travail et de la persévérance : « Je fais partie d’une génération qui a connu l’espoir né à la suite de l’indépendance de l’Algérie. Cet espoir faisait déborder d’enthousiasme et de dynamisme toute la société algérienne. J’ai le sentiment que, enfants, nous osions rêver à un bel avenir. Tout ou presque nous semblait possible ». Noureddine Melikechi a reçu de nombreuses distinctions. Il a, entre autres, été nommé, en 2011, « ambassadeur du Delaware sur Mars » par le gouverneur du Delaware. Nour. Noureddine Melikechi. Un chemin de savoir et d’espoir. Rym Khelil. Editions barzakh. 2026. 286 p. 1000 da. L’article « Nour. Noureddine Melikechi » : le récit intime du physicien algérien de la NASA est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Obi woos Onitsha voters, promises jobs, better services
items.description: …Says Nigeria needs energetic president By Vincent Ujumadu The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, on Friday drew a large crowd in Onitsha, Anambra State, as he led members of his campaign team on a roadshow and town hall meeting in the commercial city. Obi began his visit with a stop at his alma mater, Christ the King College (CKC), Onitsha, where he told students that the institution had produced three state governors and could soon produce Nigeria’s president. The three former governors he identified were Peter Odili of Rivers State, Obi himself and Willie Obiano, who succeeded him as governor of Anambra State. Addressing the students, Obi promised to improve the standard of education across the country if elected president in the 2027 general elections. His campaign train subsequently moved through Oguta Road, Upper Iweka, Head Bridge, Uga Road and Modebe Avenue before arriving at All Saints Cathedral, venue of the town hall meeting. Among those who accompanied him during the roadshow were Aisha Yesufu and other members of his campaign team. Traders at the drug market and building materials market lined the streets, dancing to campaign music, while several traders reportedly closed their shops to attend the town hall meeting. Addressing supporters at the gathering, Obi said he and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, had formed a team committed to uniting the country, tackling insecurity and corruption, and ensuring that public resources were used for the benefit of Nigerians. “Kwankwaso and I have formed a team that will unite and secure Nigeria. We will secure Nigeria, fight corruption and use public money for public good. “I assure Nigerians that from day one, they will be feeling the good impact of their country. You will know that a new team is in charge,” he said. He promised to move Nigeria from a consumption-driven economy to one centred on production, create employment opportunities and invest in critical sectors. “We cannot continue with the present situation where our children don’t have jobs because that is not the way a country should be,” he said. On healthcare, Obi advocated a system where Nigerians could access functional medical facilities without having to depend on religious institutions for treatment. He pledged to establish functional primary healthcare centres in every ward and said his proposed administration would build 10,000 healthcare centres across the country. He also promised that his administration would commence the construction of 40,000 classroom blocks from its first day in office, alongside increased investment in education and healthcare. On electricity, the former Anambra governor expressed concern over Nigeria’s power generation capacity, which he put at about 5,000 megawatts. He said his proposed administration would work towards generating, transmitting and distributing 10,000 megawatts of electricity. Obi urged Nigerians to hold him and his running mate accountable for their campaign promises, insisting that they were not making promises without understanding the country’s challenges. “We don’t want to make false promises. We are not going to tell Nigerians what we saw when we came in. We are seeing everything now and we are planning for it,” he said. He also urged voters to actively participate in the 2027 elections and protect their votes by remaining at polling units until votes were counted and results transmitted. “I want all of you to know that you are contestants in the forthcoming elections, although you are doing it through those of us that are candidates. So, on that day, sacrifice it for Nigeria,” he told the gathering. He urged voters to remain at their polling units after casting their ballots, adding that they should not be intimidated into leaving before the conclusion of the counting and result-transmission processes. Obi also called on supporters to vote for NDC candidates in the presidential, senatorial and House of Representatives elections, as well as the subsequent House of Assembly election. On the economy, he criticised the Federal Government’s handling of the removal of petrol subsidy, arguing that the policy had contributed to rising living costs and worsening hardship. He also questioned the government’s borrowing, alleging that it had accumulated more debt than previous administrations combined, while raising concerns about the implementation of successive national budgets. “Today, he has borrowed more money than all the previous governments put together. The question is, where is our money?” he asked. Obi called for a change of government in 2027, saying Nigeria needed leadership defined by competence, compassion, commitment and character. He also questioned President Bola Tinubu’s capacity to sustain the demands of the presidency, arguing that the country needed an energetic leader. “Above all, we want a government that has energy. Our current president has to go and rest because he is tired. This job requires energy and the person doing it must have energy. That is why we are begging him to go and rest,” he said. The post Obi woos Onitsha voters, promises jobs, better services appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Casablanca : un complexe pénitentiaire de 1,5 MMDH pour remplacer Oukacha
items.description: Un nouveau complexe pénitentiaire devrait voir le jour dans la province de Médiouna, en périphérie de Casablanca. Porté par la Délégation générale à l’administration pénitentiaire et à la réinsertion (DGAPR), le projet prévoit la construction de cinq établissements indépendants, destinés à remplacer la prison d’Aïn Sebaâ, plus connue sous le nom d’Oukacha. Le choix du site semble désormais se préciser. Selon les informations recueillies par Hespress , plusieurs réunions ont récemment rassemblé les responsables de la préfecture de la province de Médiouna et ceux de la DGAPR, notamment les représentants du service des équipements, ainsi que différentes administrations concernées. Au centre des discussions : les contours du projet et l’identification du terrain devant accueillir les futures infrastructures. Les responsables auraient ainsi retenu une parcelle située sur la route d'El Gara, dans la commune de Sidi Hajjaj Oued Hassar. Relevant du domaine privé de l’Etat, ce terrain s’étend sur une superficie d’environ 22 hectares. Le devenir de la prison d’Oukacha, une fois le nouveau complexe opérationnel, n’a toutefois pas encore été précisé. Des sources au sein de la DGAPR n’ont pas apporté d’éclaircissements sur ce point. Le directeur général de l’institution, Mohamed Salah Tamek, avait néanmoins confirmé devant la Chambre des représentants, lors de l’examen du projet de loi de finances, le lancement des études techniques relatives à la réalisation d’un complexe pénitentiaire à Médiouna, composé de cinq établissements et appelé à remplacer la prison actuelle. Un investissement de 1,5 MMDH Le coût global de cette opération est estimé à près de 1,5 milliard de dirhams. L’ouverture des plis de l’appel d’offres correspondant est programmée pour le 5 janvier prochain. Le projet porte sur la construction de cinq structures pénitentiaires distinctes, dont les superficies couvertes ont été définies dans les documents techniques. La première devrait s’étendre sur 42.000 mètres carrés, la deuxième sur 54.000 mètres carrés et la troisième sur 34.000 mètres carrés. Les deux dernières disposeront chacune d’une superficie couverte de 42.000 mètres carrés. Au-delà des bâtiments destinés à accueillir les détenus, le cahier des charges prévoit un dispositif de sécurité comprenant des enceintes extérieures, des miradors de surveillance ainsi que des espaces administratifs, sécuritaires et de services nécessaires au fonctionnement des établissements. Les spécifications techniques prévoient, pour chaque structure, un mur d’enceinte de 1.000 mètres de long et de sept mètres de haut, complété par cinq miradors. Ces équipements s’inscrivent dans le dispositif de sécurisation prévu pour les futures infrastructures. Des études techniques et un suivi sur 810 jours Les missions confiées aux bureaux d’études couvriront un large éventail de prestations. Elles porteront notamment sur l’élaboration des plans et des calculs d’ingénierie relatifs aux structures et aux fondations, ainsi que sur les études des réseaux électriques, d'alimentation en eau et d'assainissement. Les systèmes de prévention contre les incendies, de climatisation, de vidéosurveillance et les réseaux informatiques figurent également dans le périmètre des prestations attendues. Leur intervention ne se limitera pas à la phase de conception. Les bureaux d’études devront également assurer le suivi des différentes étapes du chantier, vérifier la conformité des travaux aux prescriptions techniques et superviser les opérations de réception provisoire et définitive. Ils seront enfin chargés de préparer les dossiers relatifs à la réalisation des différentes infrastructures et à leur équipement. La durée globale des missions est fixée à 810 jours pour chaque lot. Elle comprend 60 jours consacrés aux études techniques et 730 jours dédiés au suivi des travaux, auxquels s’ajoutent les délais liés aux opérations de réception des ouvrages. The post Casablanca : un complexe pénitentiaire de 1,5 MMDH pour remplacer Oukacha appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.description: El presidente del Gobierno y candidato del PSOE, Pedro Sánchez, ha cargado este viernes en Santiago de Compostela contra el líder del PP, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, y el presidente de Vox, Santiago Abascal, a quienes ha acusado de querer revertir las políticas de memoria democrática. “Vamos a votar en nombre de los nietos del exilio republicano”, ha proclamado, antes de asegurar que el PSOE ganará las elecciones “en memoria de esos abuelos, de esas abuelas, de sus hijos y sus hijas republicanos”. items.title: World Toilet Day: From 29% to 79%: How Upper West turned the tide against open defecation
items.description: Over a decade ago, the proportion of communities declared Open Defecation Free (ODF) in the Upper West Region stood at about 29 per cent. No toilet at home. No toilet in school. No toilet at the health facility. When nature called, people had to run to the bush, the farm or the open field. For women and girls, that walk was not just shameful; it was dangerous. For children, it meant exposure to disease. For the entire region, it meant lost dignity. But on World Toilet Day 2026, at Nandom, the region has a different story to tell. A story of 79 per cent of communities now free from open defecation. A story of a region that was once lagging behind but is now leading Ghana. The Nandom Municipal Director of Social Welfare, Naa Biligio S. Enock, speaking on behalf of the Nandom Municipal Coordinating Director, said access to safe sanitation should not depend on who a person is. “Access to safe, clean, hygienic and accessible toilet facilities should not be determined by one’s gender, age, disability, social or economic status or geographical location.” “A safe toilet is more than just a sanitation facility. It is a protection against disease, a safeguard for human dignity, a means of promoting privacy and security.” In plain language: A toilet is dignity. A toilet is safety. A toilet is health. The numbers that made the crowd clap The Upper West Regional Director of Environmental Health, Freda Naatu, said safe toilets protect the health and dignity of women and girls. “Safe toilets protect women and girls’ health, safety, dignity, and opportunity, enabling them to attend school, work, and fully participate in community development.” In 2011, the Upper West Region started with just 29 per cent of its communities declared Open Defecation Free. Today, out of 1,167 communities in the region, 938 have been declared Open Defecation Free, representing 79 per cent. Upper West is no longer lagging behind. It is leading Ghana’s rural sanitation transformation. The evidence on the ground The Project Manager of the SNV-implemented Healthy Future for All (HF4A) project, Theresa Swanzy Baffoe, said access to safe sanitation was not just a public health concern but also a matter of dignity and equal opportunity. “Access to safe sanitation is not just a public health concern, but is also about protecting human dignity and creating equal opportunities.” She said that in Nandom, the proportion of households without toilets had dropped from 37.31 per cent to just 6.92 per cent. Through the HF4A project, SNV, in partnership with the Nandom Municipal and Lambussie District Assemblies, has delivered 50 boreholes, 24 solar-powered water systems, 32 gender-friendly toilets and more than 500 handwashing stations. The project has reached 88 communities. One promise. One year. The chief who chaired the function, Ko Naa Thomas Gyireh Domapie, pledged to intensify sanitation education across Nandom’s 88 communities. “We will continue to sensitise our people more. We have about 88 communities.” He added: “So we are promising that come 2027, about this time, all the communities in Nandom will be declared Open Defecation Free.”

items.title: Oyedele urges banks to prioritise agricultural lending
items.description: …Commissions Moniepoint Abuja branch By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has urged banks and other financial institutions to make loans more affordable and accessible to businesses, particularly those operating in the agricultural sector, to stimulate productivity and economic growth. Oyedele made the call on Friday at the commissioning of the Abuja branch office of Moniepoint Microfinance Bank (MFB). He said access to affordable financing remained a major challenge for small businesses, stressing that interest rates, fees, repayment periods and the time required to secure loans must be considered in determining the usefulness of credit facilities. “We also must make business finance more affordable and more useful for many small businesses. The challenge is obtaining finance at a cost and on terms that they can sustain. “Affordability involves the interest rates, the fees that we charge, the repayment period, and time spent securing even that facility itself. All of these decide whether financing helps a business or puts it under strain,” he said. The minister said while the government had a responsibility to strengthen economic conditions to make financing more affordable, financial institutions must also contribute through efficient operations, improved risk assessment and transparent pricing. He particularly emphasised the need for increased lending to agriculture, noting that every segment of the value chain required adequate financial support. According to him, farmers need timely access to inputs and working capital, aggregators require funds to purchase produce, while processors need financing for equipment, storage and reliable supplies. He added that transporters and traders also required financial support to move agricultural products efficiently to consumers. Oyedele said appropriate financing for the sector would boost food production, reduce post-harvest losses, improve rural incomes and create employment opportunities. He, however, cautioned that agricultural lending must reflect the realities of farming, including production cycles, weather conditions and market risks. “Repayment schedules should follow production and harvest cycles. Lending decisions should recognise risks such as weather and market conditions, and partnerships with cooperatives, insurers, buyers and other credible participants can help lenders understand and manage them better,” he said. The minister urged Moniepoint to deepen its engagement with agricultural businesses and develop practical partnerships to support viable enterprises. On data protection, Oyedele called on financial institutions to strengthen safeguards around customers’ personal and financial information to protect them against fraud and other abuses. He said public confidence in the financial system depended on customers being assured that their money was safe, their information was handled responsibly and the terms of financial products were clearly explained. He also stressed the importance of customer education on protecting account credentials, identifying suspicious messages and reporting suspected fraud. According to him, financial institutions must provide accessible complaint-resolution channels and ensure customers know who is handling their complaints and when to expect a response. He said cooperation between financial institutions and regulators remained essential to sustaining confidence in the financial system as digital financial services expanded. Oyedele commended Moniepoint for establishing its Abuja office, noting that the Federal Capital Territory provided a strategic location for serving businesses and communities across the North-Central and Northern regions. “The location of this hub is significant. Abuja connects important commercial routes and provides a base for serving communities across North-Central and Northern Nigeria, including areas with substantial agricultural potential,” he said. In his remarks, the Chief Executive Officer of Moniepoint, Tunde Olofin, described the financial institution as a bank of choice, attributing its growth to its digital banking services and innovative products. He listed instant settlement for businesses and working capital loans among the products that had strengthened the bank’s appeal to customers. Olofin said the opening of the Abuja branch marked an expansion of the bank’s services beyond digital channels, providing customers with physical locations where they could receive face-to-face support and interact with business relationship managers. He said the bank planned to establish more branches in additional states to bring its services closer to customers. Olofin reaffirmed the institution’s commitment to building what he described as financial happiness for every Nigerian. Also speaking, the Managing Director of Shared Agent Network Expansion Facilities (SANEF) Limited, Uche Uzoebo, commended Moniepoint’s innovation and urged young Nigerians to contribute to national development. She said Nigerians must take responsibility for building the country rather than expecting others to do so. “I want to tell us Nigerians that we have to believe in ourselves. If we don’t build this place, nobody will build Nigeria for us,” she said. The post Oyedele urges banks to prioritise agricultural lending appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Tinubu focused on next generation, not next election, Owan-Enoh says
items.description: …Targets APC victory in all 18 Cross River LGAs By Ike Uchechukwu, Calabar The Minister of State for Industry, Senator John Owan-Enoh, has said President Bola Tinubu is focused on building a prosperous future for Nigerians rather than seeking victory at the next election. Owan-Enoh stated this on Friday at Ikom Township Stadium during the inauguration of the Cross River chapter of Project Beyond’s executive and polling unit structures for the Central and Northern Senatorial Districts of the state. He described Tinubu as a pragmatic leader whose decisions were driven by long-term national development rather than immediate political considerations. The minister likened the President’s leadership approach to that of Singapore’s founding Prime Minister, Lee Kuan Yew, whom he credited with transforming the Asian country into a global success story. “That Prime Minister didn’t look at politics the same way a politician looks at the next election. That Prime Minister looked at the next generation. “That is what President Bola Tinubu is doing,” he said. Owan-Enoh acknowledged that the President’s economic reforms had subjected many Nigerians to hardship but described the sacrifices as temporary measures necessary for economic recovery. He likened the reforms to bitter medicine that would eventually restore the country’s economic health. “That tablet is bitter. But after that bitterness, you’ll get well,” he said. According to him, Nigeria has begun experiencing economic recovery and stability after three and a half years of the administration’s policies. He said the government’s next priority was to translate the gains into prosperity and improved purchasing power for Nigerians. “Three and a half years later, recovery has started. Stability has set in, and I think for President Tinubu, the next concentration is prosperity. “The next concentration is the power of your pocket,” he said. The minister further claimed that inflation had declined to about 14 per cent, expressing optimism that it would continue to fall towards single digits. He urged Cross River residents to support Tinubu’s re-election, arguing that the state needed to maintain its influence in national decision-making. “You will need to sit at the table when decisions are taken for you to be able to put before that table what you want,” he said. Owan-Enoh said securing the state’s political relevance required a strong electoral showing for the APC in the 2027 general elections. Recalling the 2023 presidential election, he said Tinubu won in seven of Cross River’s 18 local government areas. He, however, challenged party members to work towards securing victory in all 18 local government areas in the January 16, 2027 presidential election. “In 2023, out of 18 local governments, the President won seven. “In 2027, we must leave here with a determination and a resolve that, come January 16, 2027, Mr President is going to win 18 over 18 in Cross River, and that is possible,” he said. The post Tinubu focused on next generation, not next election, Owan-Enoh says appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Prix d’Excellence du Leadership local : Bada Mbathie du Soleil primé à l’échelle du continent
items.description: Le journalisme sénégalais est à l’honneur. Bada Mbathie, du quotidien Le Soleil, figure parmi les lauréats de l’édition panafricaine 2026 du Prix d’excellence du leadership local (Pell) dans la catégorie « Articles de presse ». Les résultats ont été dévoilés ce vendredi 20 novembre par l’Observatoire international de la démocratie participative (Oidp). Placée sous l’égide de l’Union africaine, de l’Observatoire international de la démocratie participative (Oidp, Point focal Afrique) et des Cités et Gouvernements Locaux Unis d'Afrique (Cglu Afrique), cette distinction récompense les acteurs qui font avancer la gouvernance locale sur le continent. Six catégories étaient en compétition, des ministères aux jeunes créateurs, en passant par les collectivités, les chercheurs et les journalistes. Dans la catégorie des journalistes et communicants, Bada Mbathie est le seul représentant sénégalais. Il figure aux côtés de la Béninoise Kobayé Sandrine Tchobo, de la Nouvelle Tribune, primée pour les documentaires-reportages. Le texte récompensé, « Gestion du cadre de vie : Thiaroye Kaw retrouve son éclat grâce à ses jeunes », a été publié le 11 août 2025. Il suit l’association « Union progressiste de Yeumbeul Sud » dans sa lutte contre l’insalubrité, sous le slogan « Zéro déchet ». Un dimanche 3 août, le journaliste la regarde investir les ruelles de la banlieue, gilets sur le dos, gants aux mains, sacs-poubelles et pinces en bandoulière. Le reportage est écrit à hauteur d’habitants. On y croise des jeunes en sueur sous une chaleur suffocante, des chauffeurs qui glissent des pièces de monnaie, des passants qui apportent des sachets d’eau et Modou Mbacké Dieng, sexagénaire qui érige l’association en modèle à vulgariser. Bada Mbathie donne aussi la parole à Karim Bitèye, surnommé « Capitaine », qui regrette le peu d’implication des autorités locales et rappelle que les cotisations des membres financent seules le matériel. C’est là que le papier rejoint l’esprit du prix. Il montre ce que peut accomplir un quartier quand chacun s’engage pour le bien commun, sans taire les limites d’une action citoyenne laissée sans appui. Le Sénégal a d’ailleurs brillé sur plusieurs fronts. Les communes de Khombole, Cambérène, Ngor, Ngogom et Bargny ont été distinguées, tout comme Pikine Ouest, récompensée dans deux catégories. Le Dr El Hadji Rawane Ba de l’université Cheikh Anta Diop a été primé chez les enseignants-chercheurs et le lycée de Koutal a été salué chez les jeunes créateurs avec « Koutal88 ». Cette distinction de Bada Mbathie rejaillit sur toute la rédaction du Soleil. Elle rappelle aussi le rôle de la presse dans la valorisation des initiatives locales. En mettant en récit l’action des collectivités et des citoyens, le journalisme éclaire le débat public et fait connaître les bonnes pratiques. Mais encore faut-il accepter de se baisser. Il y a ceux qui passent devant les ordures sans les voir et ceux qui se baissent pour les ramasser. À Thiaroye Kaw, les jeunes l’ont fait avec leurs gants et leurs râteaux. Bada Mbathie, lui, s’est baissé pour ramasser leur histoire. Et le continent vient aujourd’hui de saluer ce geste simple et rare ; celui d’un journaliste qui regarde là où l’on ne regarde plus. Samba Oumar FALL

items.title: 2027: Our achievements will speak for us, Namadi tells voters
items.description: …Says administration needs no fresh campaign promises By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse Jigawa State Governor and All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate for the 2027 election, Malam Umar Namadi, has said his administration’s achievements in the last three years would serve as its campaign message, insisting that it does not need to make fresh promises to secure re-election. Namadi stated this on Wednesday while addressing a large crowd of APC supporters during the flag-off of the party’s campaign in the South-West Senatorial District at Jahun Local Government Area of the state. The governor said his administration had recorded achievements in agriculture, healthcare, education, electricity, job creation and other critical sectors, adding that its performance should be the basis for seeking another mandate. “We are here not to make promises. What we have done in the last three years is enough for you to put your trust in us,” he said. “Some other candidates will come to you making promises about what they will do, but for us, it is about what we have achieved in the last three years.” He reiterated his commitment to improving infrastructure, connecting communities and making life easier for residents, assuring that his administration would sustain its development agenda if re-elected. Namadi expressed satisfaction with the turnout of party members and supporters, describing it as a demonstration of confidence in the APC and its leadership. He also highlighted development projects executed by the Jigawa State and Federal Governments across the senatorial district, assuring party members that the APC would reach every town and village to mobilise support for its candidates. The governor reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to prioritising agriculture, education, healthcare, skills development, entrepreneurship and social welfare. “We will continue to give priority to agriculture, education, healthcare, skills development, entrepreneurship and social welfare because these are critical areas for building a better future for our people,” he said. On agricultural development, Namadi said his administration would sustain its partnership with the Federal Government to boost food production, strengthen food security and promote economic prosperity. “Our partnership with the Federal Government in agriculture will continue to support food production, strengthen food security and promote economic prosperity in Jigawa State and across the country. “We are determined to ensure that the benefits of these efforts reach our farmers, households and communities,” he added. Namadi urged residents of the South-West Senatorial District to turn out in large numbers on January 16 and February 6, 2027, to vote for APC candidates, from President Bola Tinubu to candidates contesting seats in the State House of Assembly. He also called for unity among party supporters, urging them to sustain what he described as the progress recorded under APC-led governments. The post 2027: Our achievements will speak for us, Namadi tells voters appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Diri’s kinsmen declare support for Dickson, NDC
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Political stakeholders and members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) from Kolokuma/Opokuma, the constituency of Bayelsa State Governor Douye Diri, have declared support for the party’s National Leader, Senator Seriake Dickson, and his political leadership. The delegation, comprising NDC candidates, stakeholders and party members from Kolokuma/Opokuma and Yenagoa Federal Constituency, made the declaration when they visited Dickson at his country home in Toru-Orua, Bayelsa State, to pay homage and demonstrate solidarity with him. The development comes as Governor Diri, who hails from Kolokuma/Opokuma, has joined the All Progressives Congress (APC). The delegation presented drinks, gifts and food items to Dickson in appreciation of his contributions to the people and his role in providing a political platform for their aspirations. Speaking during the visit, the senator representing Bayelsa West said his political journey had been driven by a commitment to justice, equity, recognition, integration and freedom for oppressed people rather than personal ambition or material gains. Dickson, who described himself as a politician motivated by a mission and a cause, said his political convictions were founded on the determination to fight for what was right, fair and beneficial to the people. He maintained that his years in public service, including his tenure as governor and senator, had been guided by the collective interest of the people rather than personal enrichment. In a statement signed by his spokesman, Steve Nwosu, the NDC leader said individual ambitions must always be subordinated to the general good, stressing that politics should be about service, responsibility, dignity and societal advancement. He said these were the values the NDC intended to promote and institutionalise as it worked towards building a different political culture in Nigeria. Dickson also acknowledged the historical significance of Kolokuma/Opokuma in the struggle for the emancipation and recognition of the Ijaw people, describing the area as a cradle of the Ijaw struggle. He recalled that the importance he attached to the area informed his decision to establish the Ijaw National Academy there. The former governor thanked the delegation for their solidarity and commitment to the NDC and the Niger Delta cause, describing the visit as a demonstration of shared values and a collective determination to advance the political and developmental aspirations of the region. Speaking on behalf of the delegation, the member representing Kolokuma/Opokuma Constituency II in the Bayelsa State House of Assembly, Dr Fafi Wisdom, assured Dickson of the continued support of political stakeholders from the area. Wisdom said the visit was organised to appreciate Dickson’s contributions to the development of Kolokuma and Yenagoa and reaffirm confidence in his leadership. He particularly commended the NDC leader for providing opportunities for indigenes of the area to contest elective positions on the party’s platform despite prevailing political challenges. He insisted that many people in Kolokuma remained appreciative of Dickson’s sacrifices, political investments and efforts to create opportunities for their people. The lawmaker also expressed confidence in the NDC’s prospects in the forthcoming elections, declaring that the party had established a presence in Kolokuma/Opokuma. He said its growing acceptance and expanding political structures were attracting attention among political opponents. Wisdom further welcomed the entry of a prominent political figure popularly known as the German Machine into the NDC, describing the development as a boost to the party’s mobilisation and grassroots engagement. He expressed optimism that the politician’s involvement would strengthen the party’s existing structures and attract more supporters ahead of the 2027 general elections. Earlier, another delegation comprising NDC candidates from Bayelsa West also visited Dickson at his country home in Toru-Orua. Led by Hon. Selekebina Saboh, the delegation presented drinks, gifts and food items to the senator in appreciation of his leadership and role in founding the NDC. They described the party as a platform that had provided them with opportunities to pursue their political aspirations. The post Diri’s kinsmen declare support for Dickson, NDC appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Coyah : l’artiste Jack Woumpack condamné à 6 mois de prison ferme
items.description: Jacques Gbignamou, alias Jack Woumpack, a été condamné ce vendredi 20 novembre 2026 par le Tribunal de première instance (TPI) de Coyah à 24 mois d’emprisonnement, dont 18 mois assortis de sursis et 6 mois de prison ferme. L’artiste a été reconnu coupable des faits d’outrage à caractère racial ou ethnique, de diffusion de nouvelles non étayées par le biais d’un système informatique et de diffusion de données de nature à porter atteinte à autrui par le biais d’un système informatique. Se réclamant proche du pouvoir, Jack Woumpack est connu pour ses sorties controversées visant certaines communautés. Récemment, dans une vidéo devenue virale sur les réseaux sociaux, l’artiste a dénoncé ce qu’il présente comme un système dans lequel l’appartenance à une communauté serait nécessaire pour bénéficier de certains avantages. Dans une autre vidéo, il s’en est vivement pris au ministre guinéen des Affaires étrangères, qu’il accuse de lui avoir refusé un passeport diplomatique qu’il affirme lui avoir été promis par le chef de l’État. items.title: Ondo orders removal of roadside logs after fatal crash
items.description: …Bans movement of timber after 7pm By Dayo Johnson, Akure The Ondo State Government has ordered the immediate removal and impoundment of timber stockpiled along roadsides across the 18 local government areas of the state following a fatal road accident that claimed three lives. The directive also prohibits the movement of logs after 7pm, with the government warning that vehicles found violating the restriction would be impounded alongside their cargo. The Senior Special Assistant to the Governor on Forestry, Bidemi Joshua Obayangban, announced the measures following the death of three persons in an auto crash at Ominla, along the Okitipupa–Ore Road. Obayangban blamed the accident on the illegal stockpiling of timber along major roads, which he said narrowed roadways and obstructed motorists’ views. In a statement, he commiserated with the families of the deceased and sympathised with others affected by the incident. He said timber dealers, loaders and transporters had repeatedly been warned against leaving felled logs beside roads, noting that the practice posed serious dangers to motorists. He also warned that loading and transporting timber at night endangered road users and provided cover for illegal logging and timber theft. “Apart from the fact that these logs are illegal, they are actively causing road accidents and were the exact cause of the fatal crash that occurred on the Okitipupa–Ore Road,” he said. According to him, stockpiling felled logs along roads and highways in the state is prohibited, while roadside and highway loading are also banned. He added that vehicles must not load or transport logs after 7pm, warning that those found violating the directive would be impounded with their cargo. “Logs already stockpiled along roads must be removed without delay,” he said. Obayangban said the Government Task Force on Forestry would work with security agencies to enforce the directives across the state, warning that offenders would face the full weight of the law. He also cautioned timber contractors, farmers and loggers against individuals or groups falsely presenting themselves as members of the forestry task force. According to the statement, the only task force recognised by the state government and the Ministry of the Environment is the one constituted by the Senior Special Assistant on Forestry. He said members of the task force carry identification cards bearing the SSA’s telephone number, which contractors and loggers can use to verify their identities. Obayangban urged timber contractors, dealers, loaders and drivers to cooperate with the government, stressing that no business activity was worth endangering human lives. He said the government was determined to keep highways across the state free from hazardous activities capable of causing fatal accidents and directed all forestry task forces to begin immediate clearance of roadside timber stockpiles. items.title: Santé reproductive et lutte contre les violences de genre : « C’est la vie ! » s’invite sur TV5MONDE
items.description: La fiction sénégalaise « C’est la vie ! », coproduite par Mediawan Africa et l’Ong Raes, est de retour sur les écrans de Tv5 Monde. Depuis le 2 novembre, la websérie et sa série mère, « C’est la vie ! Nouvelle génération », sont proposées sur Tv5 monde Afrique et la plateforme numérique Tv5 Monde+. Selon un communiqué, il sera question de santé reproductive, des droits des jeunes et les violences basées sur le genre. Lancée en 2014, la production retrouve ainsi une nouvelle vitrine internationale. En douze ans, elle s’est imposée comme l’une des fictions populaires de l’Afrique francophone, en mettant en scène, avec humour et réalisme, les histoires d’amour, les conflits familiaux, les ambitions et les choix de vie qui traversent les sociétés africaines. Diffusée à la télévision, à la radio et sur les plateformes numériques, elle a progressivement dépassé les frontières sénégalaises. Ce retour s’accompagne d’une présence renforcée sur les supports numériques. Les 71 épisodes de la « websérie » sont disponibles sur Tv5 Monde+ depuis le 4 novembre, tandis que des compilations hebdomadaires sont proposées sur « YouTube ». La série mère reprend, quant à elle, sur Tv5 Monde Afrique le 20 novembre. Outre le divertissement, « C’est la vie ! » revendique également une portée sociale. Le programme aborde notamment la santé reproductive, les droits des jeunes et les violences basées sur le genre. D’après le communiqué publié le 15 novembre par les deux coproducteurs, il compte 2,04 millions d’abonnés sur les réseaux sociaux et a enregistré 32 millions de vues et d’impressions au premier semestre 2026. Les partenaires mettent également en avant une hausse de 12 % de la fréquentation des structures de santé accompagnées. Une manière de rappeler que la fiction peut aussi devenir un outil de sensibilisation et de changement social. Pathé NIANG

items.title: Mamadou Diagna Ndiaye et moi : Itiniraire d’une personnalité atypique (
items.description: De la réussite des JOJ Dakar 2026 au legs d'une génération lumineuse… ! Il est des parcours qui ne se racontent pas uniquement à travers les fonctions exercées, les titres obtenus ou les responsabilités assumées. Ils se comprennent aussi à travers les époques qu'ils traversent, les rencontres qu'ils suscitent, les convictions qu'ils portent et les empreintes qu'ils laissent dans la mémoire collective. Le parcours de Mamadou Diagna Ndiaye appartient à cette catégorie de trajectoires singulières. Avec Dakar 2026, le Sénégal n'a pas simplement accueilli une compétition sportive internationale. Il a franchi un seuil symbolique dans son histoire et dans celle du continent africain. Pour la première fois, les Jeux Olympiques de la Jeunesse se sont installés sur une terre africaine, donnant à une nouvelle génération l'occasion de rencontrer le monde sur son propre continent. Derrière cette ambition, il y a eu des institutions, des engagements politiques, des moyens financiers, des femmes et des hommes. Il y a également eu un parcours personnel, celui d'un dirigeant qui aura consacré une part importante de sa vie au mouvement sportif et à son rayonnement international. C'est cette histoire que je souhaite brièvement raconter afin que nul n’en ignore car c’est aussi celle d’une amitié personnelle, fraternelle indéfectible, forte affectueuse et fusionnelle renforcée par les bons présages et prières de nos parents. Une exceptionnelle aventure humaine que rien ne pourra altérer… Celle d’une jeunesse résolue à arpenter le monde avec ambition, courage, pugnacité avec comme valeurs essentielles et force majeure, notre bonne éducation et instruction, nos talents, notre courage ainsi que nos idées et idéaux de jeunes déterminés à jouer une partition dans un monde qui subissait le choc de la fin des « 30 glorieuses » période faste de l’après seconde guerre mondiale (1945 – 1975). Comment un homme, au croisement du monde économique, du sport et des relations internationales, a-t-il contribué à inscrire le Sénégal dans une nouvelle séquence de l'histoire mondiale de l’Olympisme ? Ce que l'histoire retient, ce que le temps révèle, ce que les générations transmettent… Il arrive, au terme d'un parcours, que l'on éprouve le besoin de s'arrêter, de prendre du recul et de regarder le chemin parcouru. Non pour dresser un inventaire de distinctions, de responsabilités ou de réalisations, mais pour tenter de comprendre ce qui, au-delà des événements, demeure véritablement attaché à une personnalité. Le parcours de Mamadou Diagna Ndiaye invite à cet exercice. Banquier d’affaires reconnu, positionné aux confluents et affluents de la finance internationale, dirigeant sportif, acteur du mouvement olympique international et figure centrale de l'aventure olympique sénégalaise, il aura traversé plusieurs univers, parfois éloignés les uns des autres, mais reliés par un même fil conducteur : celui de l'engagement, des relations humaines, de la confection de liens stratégiques et de la recherche d'une place pour le Sénégal dans les grandes dynamiques internationales. Son itinéraire n'est pas celui d'une trajectoire linéaire. Il est fait de rencontres, d'opportunités, de convictions, de responsabilités et de paris sur l'avenir. Il témoigne aussi d'une époque où les frontières entre économie, sport, diplomatie et influence internationale sont devenues de plus en plus poreuses. Dakar 2026 : bien plus que des Jeux L'organisation des Jeux Olympiques de la Jeunesse à Dakar constitue incontestablement un moment majeur de cette histoire. Pour la première fois, le continent africain a accueilli un événement olympique. Cette première n'est pas seulement une consécration sportive. Elle représente une reconnaissance symbolique, une ouverture diplomatique et une invitation faite à l'Afrique de prendre toute sa place dans l'univers des grandes manifestations internationales. Derrière les infrastructures, les cérémonies, les compétitions et la mobilisation populaire, il y a eu une ambition collective. Celle d'un pays qui a accepté de relever un défi dont la portée dépassait largement ses frontières. Dans cette aventure, Mamadou Diagna Ndiaye aura occupé une place particulière. Son engagement dans le mouvement olympique, ses relations institutionnelles et son implication dans le projet des JOJ auront contribué à inscrire cette ambition dans la durée. Mais l'histoire ne saurait être celle d'un seul homme. Elle appartient également aux autorités publiques, aux équipes d'organisation, aux partenaires, aux sportifs, aux bénévoles et à toutes celles et ceux qui ont rendu cette aventure possible. C'est précisément dans cette articulation entre l'engagement individuel et la réussite collective que réside l'intérêt historique de Dakar 2026. L'œuvre au-delà de l'homme Une distinction, aussi prestigieuse soit-elle, récompense un parcours. Une responsabilité institutionnelle confère une place. Une réalisation d'envergure inscrit un nom dans la mémoire d'une époque. Cependant, le véritable héritage se mesure autrement. Il se mesure à la capacité des institutions à poursuivre leur mission, à la pérennité des infrastructures, à la transmission des compétences, à l'émergence de nouveaux talents et à la faculté d'une génération de transformer une expérience exceptionnelle en acquis durables. C'est ici que se situe l'un des grands enjeux de l'après-Dakar 2026. Le Village olympique, les équipements sportifs, les infrastructures d'accueil, les compétences acquises dans l'organisation de grands événements et les réseaux internationaux mobilisés devront trouver une nouvelle vocation au service du développement national. La réussite d'un événement ne devient un héritage que lorsqu'elle continue de produire des effets après que les projecteurs se sont éteints. Le legs d'une génération lumineuse Au-delà de la personnalité de Mamadou Diagna Ndiaye, cette contribution aura également voulu raconter une génération. Une génération d'hommes et de femmes qui, à différentes échelles, ont investi leurs compétences, leurs relations, leur énergie et parfois leur audace dans la construction d'une ambition nationale et africaine. Une génération qui a connu les limites des possibles, mais qui a aussi appris à les repousser. Une génération qui a compris que le rayonnement international d'un pays ne repose pas uniquement sur ses ressources naturelles, sa puissance économique ou son poids diplomatique, mais également sur sa capacité à porter des projets, à fédérer des énergies et à inspirer confiance. Dakar 2026 aura donné un visage à cette ambition. La question qui se pose désormais est celle de la transmission. Comment faire en sorte que les jeunes Sénégalais et Africains ne soient pas simplement les spectateurs d'une réussite passée, mais les acteurs des transformations à venir ? Comment transmettre les expériences, les méthodes, les réseaux et les enseignements de cette aventure à ceux qui auront demain la responsabilité de poursuivre l'œuvre ? Car une génération ne laisse véritablement son empreinte que lorsqu'elle prépare celle qui luI succède. L'homme face au jugement du temps Mamadou Diagna Ndiaye appartient désormais à une histoire qui mérite d'être documentée, interrogée et transmise. Son parcours, comme toute trajectoire humaine et institutionnelle, doit pouvoir être regardé dans sa complexité : ses réussites, ses choix, ses engagements, ses convictions, mais également les interrogations et les débats que suscitent les grandes responsabilités. L'ambition de cette contribution n'aura donc pas été de construire une légende, encore moins de figer un homme dans une image définitive. Elle aura été de restituer un itinéraire, d'en comprendre les ressorts, d'en mesurer la portée et d'en interroger les prolongements. Car les hommes passent, les fonctions changent, les circonstances évoluent. Les œuvres, elles, ne survivent que lorsqu'elles sont entretenues, prolongées et enrichies par d'autres. Et c'est peut-être là que se trouve la véritable mesure d'un parcours : non pas seulement dans ce qu'un homme aura accompli de son vivant, mais dans ce que les générations suivantes pourront encore construire à partir de son expérience. Son mot de clôture des JOJ de DAKAR 2026 en dit long : « Les Jeux auront leur histoire, les médailles leurs palmarès, les distinctions leurs archives. Mais le véritable héritage de Dakar 2026 se mesurera à ce que la jeunesse africaine osera entreprendre demain. » MDN L'homme, l'œuvre et le temps. Une trajectoire individuelle. Une ambition collective. Un héritage à transmettre. L'histoire retiendra peut-être Mamadou Diagna Ndiaye comme l'une des figures qui auront accompagné l'entrée de l'Afrique dans une nouvelle dimension de l'histoire olympique. Mais le jugement le plus important appartiendra au temps : celui qui dira si l'élan de Dakar 2026 aura véritablement contribué à ouvrir de nouvelles perspectives aux générations africaines. Car au fond, la grandeur d'une œuvre ne réside pas seulement dans le moment où elle s'accomplit, mais dans la lumière qu'elle continue de projeter sur l'avenir. Ousman Blondin DIOP Ancien Ministre Conseiller, Délégué Permanent du Sénégal auprès de l’UNESCO

items.title: French Ambassador to Ghana warns of AI threats, urges Africa not to ‘wait for the West’
items.description: French Ambassador to Ghana, Diarra Dimé-Labille, has sounded an alarm over the potential threats of Artificial Intelligence, warning that humanity could be approaching a crossroads where its ability to control the technology and determine its own destiny could increasingly come into question. She believes the dangers are too significant to ignore, insisting that Ghana and the African continent must lead the charge in shaping the future of AI and establishing safeguards to protect humanity. The Ambassador says the continent must not wait for global technology giants in the West to determine how a technology, whose consequences will affect every society, operates. Speaking during a diplomatic visit to the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), she expressed concern about how quickly AI is evolving and whether humanity is adequately prepared to manage its potential risks. “Ghana and the African countries, the European countries, and all those countries can do something together. We are responsible. There is no need to wait for others to do it for us. And it’s not only the expert or the scientific that has to deal with it. It’s also all of us as citizens,” she said. The French Ambassador to Ghana and a delegation from the embassy paid a diplomatic visit to KNUST to acquaint them with the activities of the university in promoting AI education and deployment. The visit is part of a two-day tour by the ambassador to the region to inspect projects and other infrastructure being rolled out and funded by the embassy to foster socioeconomic and technological advancements. After touring the Responsible AI Lab (RAIL) at the university, the ambassador expressed hope that AI experts in the College of Engineering were also particularly concerned about the threats of the technology despite harnessing its benefits. “It’s important for us to treat this carefully. I was definitely impressed and amazed visiting the AI lab in KNUST, and one of the first reflections when I saw all those young AI experts, they were talking about safeguard. They were talking about the need for humanity to really do the best possible to contain the threat of AI,” she said. She continued: “You are an AI expert, are you not afraid? And, they told me, it’s not because we failed to prevent this kind of threat yesterday that we cannot do it today. It’s never late. “So, seeing those young Ghanaian AI experts thinking about it, having this kind of hope, makes me, very hopeful. Those young people are definitely very committed to working in a very ethical and responsible AI.” The ambassador also participated in the opening session of the Winter School at KNUST, where she reiterated France’s commitment to strengthening scientific research, academic cooperation and innovation partnerships with African countries, particularly Ghana. Ambassador Dimé-Labille highlighted that France considers Africa an important partner in scientific advancement and is keenly concerned about developing sustainable partnerships that would foster bilateral cooperation and provide practical solutions to pressing societal challenges. Meeting with some faculty members and the governing council of the university, Ambassador Dimé-Labille emphasized deepening the cooperation between the university and the embassy. “The cooperation between the French embassy and KNUST definitely needs to continue in this way. We know that we are having this cooperation and the partnership through different initiatives,” she said. Representing the Vice Chancellor, Prof Samuel Asare Nkansah, who is a professorial member of the university council, highlighted some initiatives undertaken by the university to enhance AI education and its application. He noted that the university is ready to explore AI applications in the Sustainable Development Goals, particularly ensuring social inclusion with a focus on physical challenges.
