Maxwell Kudekor appointed World International Press Club International Affairs Secretary
items.description: JoyNews journalist Maxwell Kudekor has been appointed International Affairs Secretary of the World International Press Club (WIPC), an international media organisation committed to promoting press freedom, journalists’ rights and professional cooperation. The appointment was announced in a congratulatory message issued by the organisation’s International President, Ayrongozeb Kamal, who described Mr Kudekor’s appointment as a reflection of its confidence in his leadership, dedication and commitment to global journalism. The organisation expressed optimism that his experience and contributions would strengthen its international activities and promote solidarity among journalists across different countries. Press Freedom In its congratulatory message, the WIPC said it expected the newly appointed International Affairs Secretary to contribute towards strengthening international cooperation and advancing the organisation’s objectives. “We firmly believe that his experience, cooperation, and valuable contributions will help strengthen WIPC’s international activities and promote unity, solidarity, press freedom, journalists’ rights, and professional development worldwide,” the statement said. The organisation also expressed hope that the appointment would create new opportunities for international cooperation among media practitioners, wishing Mr Kudekor success in his new responsibilities and reaffirmed its commitment to promoting unity and solidarity within the journalism profession. Commitment Reacting to the appointment, Mr Kudekor reaffirmed his commitment to defending the rights of journalists and promoting responsible journalism. “Always ready to continue in the service of humanity. Defending the rights of journalists and responsible journalism,” he stated. The appointment places the Ghanaian journalist in an international role involving the promotion of cooperation among media professionals and the advancement of the WIPC’s stated objectives. About WIPC The World International Press Club is a Bangladesh-based international professional organisation of journalists established in 2023 to build unity among journalists worldwide while protecting their professional rights, safety, dignity and welfare. Its objectives include promoting press freedom, improving journalists’ working conditions, supporting journalists facing threats or persecution and encouraging professional development through training, conferences and international exchanges. The organisation also advocates ethical journalism, fact-checking, legal assistance for journalists and cooperation with media institutions and human rights organisations. WIPC’s constitution provides for international governing structures, national branches and regional coordination arrangements intended to facilitate cooperation among journalists across countries.

items.title: ‘I won’t disappoint you in my second term’ – Adeleke assures Osun people
items.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo As the week-long activities to usher Governor Ademola Adeleke’s second term in office took off with Jumat service, the governor has vowed not to disappoint the people of the State. Represented by the Deputy Governor, Prince Kola Adewusi, at the Oja Oba Central mosque in Osogbo, the Governor recalled the struggles and battles for the sustenance of democracy in Osun State and vowed to continue to place the interest of the public at the heart of his administration. A statement issued by his spokesperson, Olawale Rasheed, on Friday stated that the governor commended Osun people for their steadfastness, perseverance and persistent solidarity during the electioneering period, saying the state has become a national model, a symbol for people’s power as the foundation of democracy. “I won’t disappoint Osun people. I will deliver even more than my first term. I am hopeful our financial situation will soon improve with the expected resolution of the local government crisis. We will take good care of workers and all segments of the society,” the governor was quoted as saying. Earlier in his sermon, Sheikh Moruf Ishola described the recent Osun election as “unprecedented in many respects and a standout record for all students of democracy. According to him, the Osun election that re-elected Governor Adeleke broke all records in terms of its dynamics and colours, adding that “the August 15 polls defied all calculations because almighty Allah ran it. “That is why Mr Governor must not abandon God and the people. He must continue to govern with the fear of God, keep promises and serve only the interests of the people,” he submitted on behalf of the Chief Imam of Osogboland, Sheikh Musa Animasahun. The prayer session was attended by the Secretary to the State Government, Hon. Teslim Igbalaye; Osun Central Accord Senatorial candidate, Hon. Ganiyu Olaoluwa; members of the state executive council; special advisers; and top government functionaries. items.title: Quand les repères s’effondrent, préserver sa foi devient une résistance
items.description: Cloué chez moi ce vendredi 19 novembre en raison d’une fatigue physique, j’ai passé beaucoup de temps devant les chaînes d’information en continu. J’ai alors mesuré à quel point notre époque se nourrit de mensonges , de rumeurs et de médisances. Lorsque l’Homme perd ses repères moraux, il retombe dans la loi de la jungle : la raison s’efface, la conscience se tait et la déraison prend le dessus. Certains salissent par ambition politique, d’autres détournent le regard par intérêt professionnel, tandis que d’autres encore trahissent pour quelques avantages financiers. Quand la vérité devient secondaire La vérité devient secondaire dès lors que les intérêts personnels ou partisans l’emportent. La morale se marchande, la loyauté se monnaye et la dignité s’égare. Dans ces temps de confusion, préserver sa foi, sa conscience et ses valeurs représente parfois le plus difficile des combats. Car lorsque la discorde s’installe, que le mensonge devient une arme et que les repères s’effondrent, savoir prendre du recul et demeurer fidèle à ses principes constitue déjà une forme de résistance. Le Prophète Muhammad (Psl) nous a d’ailleurs enseigné cette ligne de conduite face aux périodes de troubles : « * Lorsque tu verras les gens rompre leurs engagements et perdre leur loyauté […], reste chez toi, maîtrise ta langue, attache-toi à ce que tu sais être bon, délaisse ce que tu réprouves, occupe-toi de tes propres affaires et détourne-toi de celles de la foule * » (Sunan Abi Dawud). *Azzedine Gaci est recteur de la mosquée de Villeurbanne L’article Quand les repères s’effondrent, préserver sa foi devient une résistance est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: UNICEF, Lagos raise alarm over threats to children’s rights
items.description: …As children demand free education, protection, greater say in policies By Chioma Obinna The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) and the Lagos State Government have called for stronger protection of children’s rights, warning that their welfare and fundamental rights are increasingly under threat and require concrete government action. The call was made on Friday during the commemoration of the 2026 World Children’s Day at the UNICEF Lagos Office, with the theme, “My Day. My Rights. My Future.” UNICEF Chief of Field Office, Lagos, Celine Lafoucriere, said children’s rights were facing growing threats globally, stressing the need for governments and other stakeholders to guarantee every child access to education, healthcare, good nutrition, clean water, sanitation and social protection. “Children’s rights are under pressure, they’re under threat, they’re being increasingly threatened throughout the world,” she said. Lafoucriere said UNICEF was working closely with the Lagos State Government to ensure that children’s rights were respected and accessible to all, particularly the most vulnerable. She emphasised the importance of social protection programmes, noting that the existence of rights did not automatically translate into access to basic necessities. “Having a right is one thing, but it’s not going to put food on the table,” she said, explaining that social protection interventions could help vulnerable children access education, healthcare and adequate nutrition. She added that Nigeria’s future depended largely on the attention and investment devoted to children today. “The child is the future, and the future of Nigeria is today,” Lafoucriere declared. The Lagos State Commissioner for Youth and Social Development, Mobolaji Ogunlende, said the government remained committed to promoting the welfare, protection and development of every child but acknowledged that it could not achieve the objective without the support of other stakeholders. He urged parents, schools, communities, development partners and other stakeholders to work together to create an environment where every child felt safe, valued and heard. “We must translate what we hear today into meaningful action and commitment,” he said. Ogunlende assured the children that their contributions and concerns raised during the celebration would not end with the event but would inform government policies and practical interventions. Also speaking, the Speaker of the Lagos State Children’s Parliament, Abdulsalam Anjola, called for greater involvement of children in decisions affecting their lives, insisting that their voices must be considered in the formulation of policies concerning them. He said children were better positioned to communicate their experiences, particularly in cases involving abuse and other challenges. Anjola also urged the government to increase investment in education and provide opportunities for out-of-school children. “Education is the weapon that can instigate war,” he said, while calling for effective implementation of education policies to guarantee children access to opportunities to realise their potential. He expressed optimism that investing in children would contribute to a safer Lagos, a better Nigeria and stronger communities. A 14-year-old student of Ikeja Senior High School, Ishola Moyinoluwa, also called for greater protection of children’s rights, particularly access to basic and free education. She said every child deserved the opportunity to be heard, educated and equipped for the future. Moyinoluwa, whose artwork depicted a young boy dreaming of becoming an astronaut, said children’s aspirations could become reality through parental guidance and government support. She urged parents to provide educational, moral and social guidance for their children, while calling on the government to establish platforms where young people could express their views on issues affecting their rights and future. As part of the celebration, 80 children, divided into eight groups, participated in an art project titled, “80 Children, One Future,” through which they presented their visions of the Nigeria they hoped to see. UNICEF urged adults to listen to children’s concerns and make practical commitments to address the challenges affecting them. The Permanent Secretary, Lagos State Ministry of Youth and Social Development, Pharm. Toyin Oke-Osanyintolu, also encouraged children to speak out whenever their rights were threatened. She urged them to believe in their dreams, declaring, “If you can dream it, you can do it.” Oke-Osanyintolu commended UNICEF for its continued partnership with the Lagos State Government in advancing the welfare and development of children. items.title: Mahama vows to protect Oti Region from illegal mining amid iron ore and nickel discoveries
items.description: President John Mahama says the discovery of iron ore and nickel deposits in the Oti Region presents a potential source of prosperity and job creation, but insists any decision to mine the resources must be done in a way that benefits the people of the area without destroying its serene environment. Speaking during a courtesy visit by members of the Oti Regional House of Chiefs, the President said nickel was also discovered during the search for iron ore, a mineral he described as increasingly important in the green transition because of its use in manufacturing batteries for electric vehicles. The President, however, stressed the need to protect the region’s natural environment, saying the government would not want mining activities to destroy its serene surroundings. He said, “While they were looking for iron ore, they found nickel, which has now become very important in the green transition because it’s used to make the batteries for electric vehicles. “And so, that is a potential source of prosperity and also of job creation in that area. But I want to make sure that if it is going to be mined, it is done in such a way that it will not destroy the serene environment that we have.” He said consultations would continue with traditional authorities and the youth on the discoveries. President Mahama added that if the government decides to proceed with the exploitation of the deposits, it would be done in a manner that benefits the people of the area. He also expressed satisfaction that the Oti Region had no galamsey, insisting that the government intended to maintain that status.

items.title: Mahama defends constitutional restriction on chiefs’ participation in partisan politics
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has defended the constitutional restriction barring chiefs from participating in active partisan politics, saying the provision is necessary to protect the dignity and respect of the chieftaincy institution. He said traditional rulers must remain above partisan political contests while continuing to contribute to local governance and community development. Speaking during a courtesy call by the Oti Regional House of Chiefs on Friday, November 20, 2026, the President argued that allowing chiefs to contest partisan political positions could undermine the status of the institution. “The 1992 Constitution, for very good reason, decided that chiefs should not take part in partisan politics, and it was affirmed by the Supreme Court in its interpretation of what partisan politics is,” he said. Mr Mahama questioned the appropriateness of traditional rulers competing in district assembly elections against members of their own communities. “I believe that to maintain the respect of the institution, I believe that that particular clause is appropriate because can you imagine, let’s say we’re doing district assembly elections and the whole paramount chief is standing against some small student or some butcher or some teacher or something. It doesn’t all go very well,” he said. The President, however, stressed that the restriction should not prevent chiefs from playing an active role in local governance. He said the government had maintained the constitutional provision for appointed positions on district assemblies, which provides representation for traditional authorities and other groups. Mr Mahama said the appointment criteria would ensure that chiefs, women, young people and persons with disabilities were represented in the assemblies. He urged traditional authorities to nominate representatives who would participate in assembly discussions on their behalf and report back to them on decisions taken. The President also encouraged chiefs to work closely with district chief executives and monitor how public funds allocated to district assemblies were utilised. He said traditional authorities were well placed to identify the development needs of their communities and should help guide local authorities in selecting projects that respond to those priorities.

items.title: Ooni urges FG to revive, protect textile industry
items.description: …Calls for prioritisation of Nigerian fabrics, investment in local production By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo The Ooni of Ife, Oba Adeyeye Ogunwusi, has called on the Federal Government to revive and protect Nigeria’s textile industry as part of efforts to strengthen the nation’s economic growth and development. The monarch also urged textile unions to deploy all necessary measures to safeguard the industry and encourage the patronage of locally produced fabrics. Oba Ogunwusi, represented by Olori Aderonke Adeyeye, made the call on Friday at the 38th Annual National Education Conference of the National Union of Textile, Garment and Tailoring Workers of Nigeria (NUTGTWN) and the Nigeria Textile, Garment and Tailoring Employers’ Association in Ile-Ife, Osun State. Commending the unions for organising the conference to educate their members, the monarch said an informed labour union was essential to the survival of democracy and the development of the nation. He said stakeholders must work together to restore the country’s textile industry, revive moribund mills and make locally manufactured fabrics a source of national pride. “It is important for stakeholders to protect our industry. Let us prioritise our own fabrics. Let us revive our textile mills. Let us make Made in Nigeria a badge of pride, not an apology. “We must honour labour. Every tailor, every cutter, every employer deserves dignity, fair pay and respect. Labour is not servitude; labour is nation-building. “Let us raise a new generation. Teach them craft, teach them the business, teach them discipline. Do not let this knowledge die with us,” he said. The Ooni further stressed that the survival of democracy was closely linked to economic prosperity, respect for workers and the protection of local industries. “Democracy cannot stand on empty stomachs. It cannot stand where labour is not respected. It cannot stand where industry is allowed to die. A nation that abandons its artisans abandons its future,” he added. Earlier, NUTGTWN President, Comrade Peter Godonu, urged the Federal Government to translate its commitment to industrialisation into concrete policies and investments capable of reviving the country’s struggling textile industry. Godonu said Nigeria could no longer afford to celebrate the potential of its textile sector while factories remained closed, production capacity declined and imported products continued to dominate the domestic market. He said the union would sustain its advocacy for policies that promote industrialisation, local production, decent work and the revival of the textile and garment industry. “Our Union will therefore continue to intensify its advocacy and campaign for sustainable industrialisation, local production, decent work and the revival of the textile and garment industry. “We remain available to partner with the Federal Government, state governments, employers and other stakeholders in developing and implementing practical solutions to these challenges,” he said. The NUTGTWN president noted that Nigeria possessed several advantages that could support the rebuilding of a competitive textile and garment industry. These, he said, included a large domestic market, cotton-growing potential, abundant labour, technical expertise, a vibrant fashion and garment-making industry, a youthful population and access to the wider African market through the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA). He, however, said political will, policy consistency, investment and strategic coordination were necessary to harness these opportunities and restore the sector to productivity. items.title: Bono Regional Minister warns MMDCEs against neglecting district security responsibilities
items.description: The Bono Regional Minister, Joseph Addae Akwaboa, has warned Metropolitan, Municipal and District Chief Executives (MMDCEs) against neglecting their security responsibilities, urging them to prioritise the effective functioning of District Security Councils (DISECs) to prevent local security threats from escalating. He said MMDCEs, as chairpersons of their respective District Security Councils, must ensure regular meetings, proper documentation of deliberations and prompt escalation of security concerns requiring regional or national intervention. Mr Akwaboa gave the directive on Thursday, November 19, 2026, at a joint workshop for the Bono, Bono East and Ahafo Regional Security Councils (REGSECs) and MMDCEs in Sunyani. The workshop, organised by the National Security Council Secretariat, was aimed at strengthening understanding and implementation of the Security and Intelligence Agencies Act, 2026 (Act 1168). Addressing participants, the Bono Regional Minister stressed that security must be treated as an integral part of local governance rather than an issue left exclusively to security agencies. He said development planning and implementation could not be separated from the security environment within which communities operate. “I wish to emphasise that security must be mainstreamed into our local governance mandate. Development, planning and implementation cannot be divorced from the security environment within which they are expected to operate,” he stated. Mr Akwaboa explained that MMDCEs occupied strategic positions in Ghana’s decentralised security architecture because of their proximity to local communities, placing them in a position to identify emerging threats and facilitate timely responses. He said District Security Councils remained important platforms for detecting warning signs, assessing local security dynamics and referring matters requiring higher-level intervention. The minister consequently called for stronger institutional relationships between Regional Security Councils and District Security Councils through regular engagement, timely communication and structured information sharing. He identified chieftaincy disputes, land conflicts, communal tensions and other localised threats as security vulnerabilities requiring continuous monitoring and proactive intervention. Mr Akwaboa said the effective implementation of Act 1168 would further strengthen the country’s security architecture by clarifying institutional mandates, operational responsibilities and accountability mechanisms. He described the legislation as a landmark in Ghana’s security sector reforms, providing a comprehensive legal framework for the organisation, coordination and oversight of national security and intelligence functions. He maintained that a common understanding of the law among regional and district authorities was necessary to avoid institutional misunderstandings and operational lapses. “A harmonised understanding of the legal framework will promote consistency in decision-making, enhance inter-agency coordination, improve information flow and minimise the possibility of administrative and operational lapses that could compromise our collective security,” he said. The minister also urged participants to uphold confidentiality, professionalism, integrity and accountability in the handling of security information. Meanwhile, the Deputy National Security Coordinator in charge of Operations, Major General Williams Azure Ayamdo (Rtd), called for improved intelligence sharing and coordinated responses to security threats across the three regions. He warned that challenges confronting the regions could escalate when early warning signs are overlooked, information is delayed, or institutional responses are fragmented. He urged REGSECs and assembly security councils to identify emerging threats, assess their implications and facilitate timely interventions before local incidents developed into wider security challenges. He also called for greater cooperation among the three regions and encouraged traditional authorities and community leaders to support efforts at identifying local tensions and promoting peaceful dispute resolution.

items.title: 2027: Obi urges Nigerians to defend their votes
items.description: By Nwabueze Okonkwo ONITSHA — Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has urged Nigerians to turn out en masse for the January 16, 2027 presidential election and defend their votes against electoral manipulation. Obi made the call on Friday at the NDC town hall meeting and presidential campaign rally held at All Saints Anglican Church Cathedral, Onitsha, Anambra State. He said Nigerians should regard election day as an opportunity to make a sacrifice for the country by coming out to vote and remaining at polling centres to protect their ballots. According to him, whoever emerges winner in a free, fair and transparent election should be supported by all Nigerians. The former Anambra State governor, however, vowed to resist any attempt to manipulate the results in favour of any political party, saying he would not accept a repeat of what he described as irregularities that characterised the 2023 presidential election. “We are going to match them fire for fire if they attempt to rig the election as usual, and we are going to block all loopholes to ensure that our votes count. “The idea is for the right winner to emerge in a free and fair election. Nothing more, nothing less. Personally, I would like to win in a transparent election,” he said. Obi also criticised the borrowing policy of the President Bola Tinubu administration, alleging that trillions of dollars had been borrowed between 2023 and 2026 without sufficient investment in productive sectors of the economy. He warned that another four-year term for the administration after the 2027 election could worsen the country’s economic situation. At the rally, Senator Victor Umeh, representing Anambra Central Senatorial District; NDC candidate for Idemili North/South Federal Constituency, Engr. Eric Anyamene; member representing Onitsha North II in the Anambra State House of Assembly, Hon. Pat Okafor; the party’s Anambra State Deputy Chairman, Barr. Chugbo Enwezor; and Chief Ikenna Victor Egbuna, SAN, expressed confidence that the party would win the presidential, National Assembly and state assembly elections in 2027. items.title: 2027: Court sacks ADC governorship candidate in Adamawa
items.description: The Federal High Court in Abuja on Friday ordered the removal of Tukur Ribadu as the 2027 Adamawa governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC). Justice Obiora Egwuatu, in a judgment, held that Mr Omar Suleiman, who won the majority of the valid votes cast in the primary election of the party, was unlawfully substituted by Ribadu. Justice Egwuatu ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to immediately restore Suleiman as the rightful candidate of the party. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Suleiman, a cousin of former Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Babachir Lawal, was said to have initially emerged as the ADC’s candidate in the Adamawa primary. However, he was later replaced by Ribadu. Dissatisfied, Suleiman filed a suit marked FHC/ABJ/C’S/1751/2026 before Justice Egwuatu to challenge his unlawful substitution. He prayed the court to order the ADC to forward his name to the electoral umpire as a valid candidate of the party. He also prayed the court to compel INEC to publish his name as the candidate of the party. Delivering the judgment, Justice Egwuatu held that Suleiman could only be replaced as a candidate if he had formally and voluntarily withdrawn from the race or died. He ruled that since Suleiman had neither withdrawn nor died, his replacement was illegal, null and void. The judge consequently ordered INEC to immediately restore his name as the ADC governorship candidate for Adamawa State in the forthcoming governorship poll. (NAN) The post 2027: Court sacks ADC governorship candidate in Adamawa appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Vandalism, illegal connections threaten Kano water supply
items.description: Over 45 pipeline repairs completed, says commissioner By Hadiza Yusuf KANO — The Kano State Government has warned residents against vandalism, illegal connections and other activities capable of damaging public water infrastructure and disrupting the supply of drinking water across the state. The Commissioner for Water Resources, Dr Dahiru Muhammad Hashim, gave the warning at a press conference in Kano on Friday while briefing journalists on the progress of ongoing rehabilitation of water facilities and restoration of supply to communities. Hashim said the ministry had identified cases of unauthorised connections to water pipelines, vandalism, indiscriminate drilling around major water lines and improper handling of distribution valves. He added that some water pipes had also been damaged by construction activities, refuse burning and other activities around drainage channels. “We appeal to the general public to cooperate with the Ministry in protecting water infrastructure. Our assessment has identified cases of unauthorised tapping of pipelines, vandalism and damage to pipes crossing drainage channels,” he said. The commissioner urged residents, contractors and those executing construction, road and drainage projects to consult relevant authorities before embarking on activities that could affect water pipelines. He also called on residents to promptly report burst pipes, leakages, suspected vandalism and illegal connections to the appropriate authorities. According to him, the restoration of water supply has exposed weaknesses in some old pipelines, many of which had remained without regular water flow for several years. He explained that the return of water pressure to the distribution network had resulted in leakages and pipe bursts in some locations, necessitating urgent repairs and replacement of damaged infrastructure. Hashim disclosed that the ministry had completed more than 45 repair and replacement interventions across different parts of the metropolis. The affected areas include Goron Dutse, Jakara, Kofar Ruwa, Kurmi, Dukawa, Kofar Wambai, Fagge, Club Road, Tudun Wada, Gidan Zakka, Gabari, Koki, Mandawari and Sharada. He said the interventions involved replacing damaged asbestos-cement pipes, fixing leaking PVC pipelines, installing valves and repairing faulty connections. The commissioner further disclosed that water had been pumped from Challawa Water Works to the Goron Dutse reservoirs, which have a reported capacity of 42.5 million litres, before being released into the distribution network. He listed communities that had received water to include Goron Dutse, Gwammaja, Jakara, Kofar Mazugal, Muskwani, Kofar Wambai, Mandawari, Fagge, Tudun Wada, Gama, Kofar Ruwa and Alfindiki, among others. Hashim said the government was also working to improve access through the installation of public standpipes in communities where household water connections had yet to be fully restored. “Protecting water facilities is a responsibility we all share, and the cooperation of residents is vital to sustaining the improvements made in restoring water supply across Kano,” he said. items.title: Tinubu Must Stay group set to unveil presidential library, reform observatory
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Tinubu Movement for Sustainable Governance Foundation TMS, popularly known as Tinubu Must Stay, has announced plans to establish a National Reform Documentation and Impact Observatory, a public digital policy archive and a possible future presidential library for President Bola Tinubu. Chairman of the Board of Trustees and National Coordinator of the group, Malam Kashifu Inuwa Abdullahi, disclosed this on Friday during the commissioning of its National Secretariat in Abuja. He said the records would start with Tinubu’s years as Governor of Lagos State between 1999 and 2007, then cover policy developments under successive administrations, his national political career and his presidency from 2023. According to him, the archive would span public revenue administration, infrastructure, investment, education, economic management, digital transformation and institutional development. Students, researchers, historians, policymakers and ordinary citizens would be given access to original documents, implementation records, economic data and independent assessments. Inuwa said the library, the observatory and the archive remained long-term aspirations that would need feasibility studies, sustainable funding, proper governance and professional archival standards. “History serves future generations when it preserves evidence, not merely admiration,” he said. He added that the documentation must make room for achievements, implementation difficulties, independent criticism and lessons learned. The announcement came with a membership claim. Inuwa said the group, formally launched on October 1, 2026, had recorded 61,093 validated members within seven weeks across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). He said the group had representation in 730 of the country’s 774 local government areas, about 94 per cent geographical coverage. Its digital database also captures 4,750 wards and 22,584 polling units. Inuwa said 65 per cent of members, roughly 40,000 people, were aged between 18 and 34, while the membership was 65 per cent men and 35 per cent women. “The most remarkable feature of our membership is its youthful composition. This is not merely a demographic statistic. It places a profound responsibility upon our institution,” he said. He said young Nigerians needed more than a seat in political conversations, naming quality education, employable skills, technology, finance and markets as what would turn the country’s demographic potential into prosperity. To that end, the group would run grassroots entrepreneurship workshops, digital skills training, mentorship programmes and policy dialogues. “Today, we are not merely opening an office. We are opening a new chapter in our responsibility to Nigeria,” he said. Inuwa said the secretariat would serve as a centre for research, civic engagement, youth empowerment and the documentation of policies and institutions shaping national development. He insisted that the group intended to outlive the 2027 general elections, even though it openly backs the President’s Renewed Hope Agenda. He said it would encourage evidence-based assessment of government policies, including their implementation challenges and social consequences. He acknowledged that the administration’s changes to petrol subsidies, foreign exchange management and fiscal policy had drawn mixed reactions, with some Nigerians seeing them as necessary to fix long-standing structural weaknesses and others worried about implementation and hardship in households. “Reform is not an end in itself. Its purpose is to improve the lives of people,” he said. On voter readiness, Inuwa said the group’s records showed that 81 per cent of respondents already held Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs), 11 per cent had yet to collect theirs and six per cent were not registered to vote. The remaining two per cent, he said, required reconciliation. He cautioned that large membership figures did not automatically translate into effective grassroots structures or measurable results. “Our responsibility is to convert organisational reach into meaningful public value. We must move from membership registration to meaningful participation, from participation to capability, and from capability to opportunity,” he said. Inuwa said the group would spend its first 90 days assessing operational capacity, developing programme standards and setting realistic targets before publishing measurable commitments. He stressed that it was independently established, with its own leadership, governance structures and membership system, despite its declared support for the President. He urged the public to judge the organisation by its contributions to civic education, economic empowerment and sustainable development, not by membership figures or political declarations. “A building can be completed with bricks, cement and steel. An institution must be built with integrity, competence, discipline, trust and a commitment to service,” he said. Turning to the approaching elections, Inuwa expressed concern over reports of political intimidation, attacks on political gatherings and inflammatory public rhetoric. He condemned political thuggery and violence, irrespective of who was involved, and asked security agencies to investigate incidents impartially. He called on political parties, civic organisations, the media and security institutions to promote peaceful participation, accurate information and respect for opposing views, and urged members to reject intimidation and misinformation. “Political differences must never become a justification for violence. No political ambition is worth the life of an innocent Nigerian,” he warned. The post Tinubu Must Stay group set to unveil presidential library, reform observatory appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Migrations : Dakar lance un cadre de coopération pour l’Afrique de l’Ouest
items.description: Réunis à l'hôtel Azalaï, les ministres de la région ont ouvert vendredi le segment ministériel d'une conférence appelée à aboutir à une Déclaration de Dakar et à une Feuille de route régionale. Faire de la mobilité humaine un chantier commun plutôt qu'une somme de réponses nationales : c'est le pari du « processus de coopération sur les questions migratoires en Afrique de l'Ouest », officiellement lancé ce vendredi 20 novembre 2026 à Dakar. Les ministres de la région se sont retrouvés à l'hôtel Azalaï pour la phase politique d'une conférence préparée de longue date, en présence de la directrice générale de l'Organisation internationale pour les migrations (OIM), Amy Pope. Retenu hors du territoire par des obligations imprévues, le ministre de l'Intégration africaine, des Affaires étrangères et des Sénégalais de l'Extérieur, Cheikh Niang, a confié l'ouverture des travaux au ministre de la Justice, Garde des Sceaux, Me Moussa Sarr. Devant les chefs de délégation, les diplomates, les organisations régionales et internationales et les partenaires techniques et financiers, ce dernier a d'abord choisi de replacer la question dans le temps long de la région. « Bien avant que nos frontières ne soient tracées, les peuples de l'Afrique de l'Ouest allaient déjà d'un royaume à l'autre, au gré du commerce et de la quête du savoir. La mobilité est inscrite dans notre histoire ; elle a façonné nos familles comme nos cités. Mais lorsque l'espoir d'une vie meilleure se brise au large de nos côtes, elle devient un drame qui interpelle chacun de nos Etats », a-t-il déclaré. Prévention et fermeté face aux passeurs Le ministre a ensuite rattaché la démarche à la politique du chef de l'État, Bassirou Diomaye Faye, dont il a transmis le salut aux participants. « Le Président de la République a fait de la prévention de la migration irrégulière une priorité, en instituant un programme budgétaire spécial qui lui est consacré. Il a également appelé à sanctionner avec sévérité les réseaux de passeurs, ces « marchands d'illusions » qui exposent notre jeunesse à des périls mortels », a-t-il rappelé, avant d'ajouter que la conférence « prolonge cette vision en l'inscrivant dans une démarche régionale ». Cette réunion ministérielle fait suite à deux jours de travaux menés par des experts, des points focaux nationaux et des techniciens, salués par Me Sarr pour leur « rigueur » et leur « détermination ». Leurs échanges ont permis, selon lui, d'établir un diagnostic partagé des dynamiques migratoires de la région. Le ministre a aussi remercié l'OIM, dont l'appui technique et l'expertise ont été « déterminants », des consultations nationales jusqu'à l'organisation de la conférence. Un cadre « durable et évolutif » Pour le Garde des Sceaux, ce processus, engagé il y a plusieurs mois et animé par le Sénégal, traduit une volonté politique claire. « Il répond à la volonté des Etats ouest-africains d'assumer pleinement la gouvernance des migrations, à travers un cadre régional durable et évolutif, fondé sur le dialogue politique et les échanges techniques », a-t-il expliqué. L'objectif, a-t-il précisé, est de « bâtir ensemble un espace de coopération renforcée, capable de rapprocher nos priorités nationales et de favoriser des réponses concertées, adaptées aux réalités de la mobilité dans les pays d'origine, de transit, de destination ou de retour ». Trois priorités se dégagent des travaux des experts : renforcer la gouvernance régionale de la mobilité humaine, protéger effectivement les migrants tout au long des routes migratoires, et valoriser la mobilité comme facteur d'intégration et de développement durable. Elles doivent servir de socle à la Déclaration de Dakar, qui fixera les principes directeurs de la coopération. Une Feuille de route régionale la complétera, en détaillant les actions prioritaires, les responsabilités de chacun ainsi que les mécanismes de suivi et de coordination. Le rôle de la justice Garde des Sceaux, Me Sarr a tenu à souligner la dimension judiciaire du dossier. « La lutte contre le trafic illicite de migrants et la traite des personnes suppose une entraide judiciaire efficace entre nos Etats », a-t-il affirmé, estimant que la pleine efficacité des futurs instruments dépendrait du concours de la justice. Il a conclu son intervention par un appel à passer à l'action : « Il nous revient désormais de traduire ces orientations techniques en réponses politiques collectives, au service d'une migration sûre, ordonnée et régulière, conforme aux aspirations légitimes de nos peuples. »

items.title: St John’s Hospital CEO Dr Maame Yaa Afriye named Outstanding Corporate Woman at 2026 Ghana Women Awards
items.description: The Chief Executive Officer of St John’s Hospital and Fertility Centre, Dr Maame Yaa Afriye, has been named Outstanding Corporate Woman at the 2026 Ghana Women Awards. She received the award at a ceremony held at the University of Professional Studies, Accra (UPSA) Auditorium on Saturday, November 14, 2026. Dr Afriye was recognised for her leadership and contributions to healthcare management and service delivery. The 2026 Ghana Women Awards brought together 23 women from various sectors, including healthcare, business, entertainment, media, engineering, sports and the security services, to recognise their contributions to society. Other award recipients included the President of the Greater Accra Markets Association, Mercy Naa Afrowa Needjan, who received the Legendary Woman Award, and the Chief Executive Officer of Hasaacas Ladies FC, Dr Evelyn Nsiah Asare, who was named Changemaker of the Year. Dr Afriye is a trained pharmacist with a Bachelor of Science degree in Pharmacy from the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST). She also holds a PhD in Health Policy and Management from the University of Ghana Business School, an MBA in Health Services Management, a Postgraduate Diploma in Business Administration and a Postgraduate Certificate in Supply Chain and Human Resource Management. She has also co-authored research publications on customer relationship management and patient satisfaction, as well as the experiences of working mothers with exclusive breastfeeding in Ghana. As head of St John’s Hospital and Fertility Centre, Dr Afriye has overseen efforts to improve the facility’s operations, infrastructure, technology and patient care. The hospital provides a range of general and specialist healthcare services, including fertility care, urology, surgery, dermatology, dental services, ear, nose and throat (ENT) care, home care and laboratory services. The latest recognition adds to several honours Dr Afriye has received in the healthcare sector. In 2024, she was named Most Outstanding Female in Healthcare and Administrative Excellence at the Corporate Ghana Hall of Fame Awards.

KEY FIGURES 7.9K people displaced in Haiti since mid-October 3.2M people could face crisis-level food insecurity in Guatemala 93K people affected by El Niño-related rains in Ecuador HAITI: VIOLENCE & DISPLACEMENT Escalating armed violence across the country is deepening humanitarian needs and restricting access, particularly in densely populated areas of the capital, Port-au-Prince. Since mid-October, violence in Croix-des-Bouquets, on the capital’s outskirts, has displaced about 2,000 people. Nearly 90 per cent are staying with host families and the rest in five informal sites. In late October, attacks in Arcahaie and Cabaret, north-west of the capital, displaced more than 5,900 people. Each new wave puts more strain on stretched host communities. Violence killed an estimated 4,200 people nationwide between January and September, and some 1.5 million people remain displaced. The UN continues to call for the protection of civilians and for safe access to health facilities, schools and other essential services. CENTRAL AMERICA: FOOD SECURITY El Niño-related drought is deepening hunger in Central America’s Dry Corridor, where families are running out of food after a failed harvest. An Oxfam assessment of 354 communities in Guatemala, Honduras and El Salvador found that nearly 8 in 10 maize-producing households lost 75 to 100 per cent of their crop this year. Most now have food reserves for three weeks or less. The drought is also cutting rural incomes: the region’s sugar harvest, a key source of seasonal work, could fall by up to 21 per cent. Projections show about 3.2 million people in Guatemala and 1.8 million in Honduras facing Crisis (IPC Phase 3) or worse levels of food insecurity, while up to 249,000 people in El Salvador could face food insecurity. SOUTH AMERICA: EL NIÑO El Niño-related rains are worsening along South America’s Pacific coast. In Ecuador, the number of people affected is 93,000 as of 18 November, up from about 65,000 a week earlier, according to the National Secretariat for Risk Management (SNGR). Of these, 36,729 have lost their homes or livelihoods. The rains have led to 16 deaths, damaged more than 25,600 homes, affected over 2,280 schools and 13,000 hectares of crops, and reached all 24 provinces. The National Institute of Meteorology and Hydrology (INAMHI) forecasts heavier rain through 21 November. In northern Peru, overflowing streams have cut off several communities in Tumbes, and forecasters warn the Piura River could rise. On 19 November, authorities placed nine Piura and Tumbes provinces under red alert. REGIONAL: HEALTH ALERTS Measles and malaria are spreading across the region as gaps in immunization and disease control persist. As of 13 November, PAHO had confirmed 58,213 measles cases and 82 deaths in the Americas this year, more than four times the number for the same period in 2025. Guatemala accounts for most of them, with more than 34,700 cases and 53 deaths. Bolivia, Mexico and the United States have now lost their measles elimination status. Panama has recorded more than 6,700 malaria cases, mainly in the East Panama, Guna Yala and Darién health regions. They include an outbreak of 161 cases in Ancón, an area of the capital, Panama City, where malaria is not endemic. On 16 November, the Ministry of Health declared a national health alert.

De ellas, 36.729 perdieron su vivienda o medios de vida. Las lluvias causaron 16 víctimas mortales, dañaron más de 25.600 viviendas, afectaron más de 2.280 escuelas y 13.000 hectáreas de cultivos, y llegaron a las 24 provincias. En el norte de Perú, el desborde de arroyos aisló a varias comunidades en Tumbes, y los meteorólogos advierten que el río Piura podría crecer. items.title: Trump urges Nvidia to give Jensen Huang ‘second chance’
items.description: US President Donald Trump on Friday called for chip giant Nvidia to reinstate disgraced former CEO Jensen Huang after he resigned over extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. “I would love to see him be back. You have one of the truly most brilliant minds in the world, and where is he going to go?” Trump told reporters. “I think that I would love to see Jensen be given a second chance.” Huang resigned last week as chief of Nvidia, a company at the center of the AI revolution, after revelations of an affair with an alleged Chinese spy who may have funneled restricted chips to that country. Reports of at least two further affairs emerged after that initial report, with US intelligence said to be aware of the possibility of the alleged Chinese espionage. Trump defended Huang as “a good man” who “made some bad decisions.” “I’d like to see Jensen make a big apology and go back because he created something with Blackwell,” he said, referring to the most advanced chips designed by Nvidia. The US president also appeared to directly contradict his own treasury secretary, saying he had spoken to China’s President Xi Jinping about Huang during a summit earlier this week. “I did discuss that with President Xi, and he said, ‘Oh, brilliant, brilliant! He’s a brilliant man,'” said Trump. Earlier in the day, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Trump had not discussed Huang with Xi during the meeting in Shenzhen. Trump advocated for Nvidia to take back Huang as their CEO “if they were smart.” Huang has offered to return to the company, a move the chip giant’s board has rejected. Board chair Harvey Jones said in an earnings call this week that “the Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” – ‘Must stay ahead’ – Earlier, Bessent had spoken at length about the AI race with China in comments to US broadcaster CNBC. Speaking about the Trump administration’s support for the domestic AI sector, Bessent stressed that the United States “must stay ahead” of China in that realm. “Our best protection against the foreign SI and exploits by foreign actors is for our labs to maintain their substantial lead, and in effect, they are our shield against SI,” he said, using the government’s preferred SI, or “super intelligence.” “There’s no turning back on this. What we have to do is make sure that our labs maintain their leads through their continued innovation, through their access to the best chips, and through smart policy.” Bessent said Trump and Xi had agreed on certain guardrails on the use of AI in the military domain. “President Trump and President Xi agreed that humans should always be involved in any military decisions that SI makes, and the SI should not be allowed to be autonomous for major military actions,” he said. On the threat of AI-enabled cyberattacks, Bessent again stressed that the best defense his country had was to allow its AI companies “to continue at the frontier and to provide us with the best defense against these other models.” The post Trump urges Nvidia to give Jensen Huang ‘second chance’ appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ‘If a mother’s tears could bring back a child’ – Javits’ mother breaks down during tribute
items.description: The mother of 15-year-old Badu Nkansah Frimpong, popularly known as Javits, broke down in tears during the reading of her tribute at his funeral in the Bronx, New York, as she struggled to come to terms with the loss of her only child. The tribute, which was read on her behalf at the funeral on Friday, November 20, recounted her pain over the death of the son she had carried, nurtured and prayed for. Standing beside the reader, Javits’ mother, Doris, became visibly emotional and broke down at the end of the reading. In the message, she described Javits as her only son, her only child and her greatest blessing, saying that although distance separated them when he travelled to the United States to live with his father, their emotional bond remained strong. She recalled their conversations and the dreams he shared with her, particularly his ambition to study hard, become a doctor and one day return to Ghana to take care of her and help less privileged people in their community. “You told me that you wanted to study hard, become a doctor and return one day to take good care of me and help the less privileged in our community in Ghana,” the tribute read. She said those words had become the foundation of her hopes and daily prayers, adding that she had imagined the day she would proudly call him “Doctor”. ‘Mema mo yaakor’ – New York City Major, Zohran Kwame Mamdani, in Akan language, pays tribute to 15-year-old Javits at funeral in the US. Full tribute of @NYCMayor. https://t.co/lu913DMo88 — Kenneth Awotwe Darko (@TheKennethDarko) November 20, 2026 The mother said she had looked forward to watching her son fulfil his ambitions and growing old with the comfort of knowing that he had achieved his dreams. But his death, she said, had abruptly ended a future they had imagined together. “My son, what hurts most is not just that you are gone, but everything you were yet to become. Your dreams, your laughter, your kindness and the beautiful future we imagined together have all been taken away,” she said. In one of the most emotional passages, she expressed the depth of a mother’s grief over the loss. “If a mother’s tears could bring back a child, I would have cried you back into my arms. If love could defeat death, you would still be here,” the tribute read. She ended by assuring her son that he would remain in her heart and that she would carry his dreams and memories for the rest of her life. “Sleep well, my only son. My heart has lost its greatest treasure,” she said. Javits was born on April 29, 2011, and moved from Ghana to the United States in 2025 to join his father and pursue his education. He aspired to become a doctor and serve in the United States military. He was fatally shot in the Bronx on October 29, 2026, aged 15.

items.title: Nasarawa attracts $2.3bn investments in seven years — Abdullahi
items.description: Records 21 reforms, 11 PPP projects worth ₦93bn By John Alechenu ABUJA — Nasarawa State has attracted more than $2.3 billion in investments over the past seven years following reforms and institutional development aimed at making the state more competitive and investor-friendly. The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Nasarawa Investment and Development Agency, Ibrahim Abdullahi, disclosed this at the 13th World Public Relations Forum 2026 in Abuja. Abdullahi said the investments cut across agriculture, solid minerals, retail, commercial activities, manufacturing, agro-processing and education. He added that the state also implemented 11 public-private partnership (PPP) projects valued at about ₦93 billion within the period. According to him, the achievements were the outcome of seven years of reforms and deliberate institution-building under Governor Abdullahi Sule, rather than publicity campaigns or political slogans. Recounting the beginning of the process, Abdullahi said he was invited into the Nasarawa State public service seven years ago, when Governor Sule appointed him as economic adviser. He said the assignment was to develop the state’s investment profile and position it as an attractive destination for investors. He thanked the organisers of the forum for recognising Governor Sule with an honour presented a few days earlier. Abdullahi said one of the first lessons from the assignment was the need to establish the necessary structures before embarking on investment promotion. “So we could not go out and invite people to come to Nasarawa State without building any framework around it. That is to say that you cannot communicate something that is not there. You cannot communicate something that hasn’t been built. So, we put our heads down and began to build,” he said. He explained that the state’s vision, as contained in the Nasarawa Economic Development Strategy, was to make it one of Nigeria’s most competitive states through improved and accelerated economic growth that would translate into better living conditions for residents. Under the strategy, he said, the government implemented more than 21 reforms focused on improving the business environment and making the state attractive to investors. He said the reforms were designed to guarantee a conducive business climate, competitive returns on investment and improved general welfare for residents. According to him, the measures included the digitisation of revenue administration and improvements in the state’s fiscal and financial management framework. Abdullahi said the reforms provided the foundation for the state to confidently promote its investment opportunities to local and international investors. He noted that investors were attracted not by impressive speeches but by predictability, transparency, good returns and a government that honoured its commitments. The investment agency chief said the experience offered important lessons to other state governments and public relations professionals, stressing that investment attraction should begin with building the necessary structures rather than merely branding a destination. He also highlighted the importance of purpose in communication, saying communicators must be clear about the objectives they seek to achieve. “Do I want to communicate to build or destroy? Once you have that conviction and a sense of purpose, it guides how you even communicate your message,” he said. On reputation management, Abdullahi said credibility was essential to attracting and retaining investors, adding that reputation required deliberate efforts to establish and sustain. “Your reputation is not just earned, you have to build it,” he said. He identified courage and collaboration as other important ingredients for success, noting that people and institutions seeking meaningful progress must be willing to pursue new ideas and take bold decisions. “There is no price tag for the best idea. Everywhere around the world, everyone who is succeeding has had to show a remarkable amount of zeal and courage,” he said. The post Nasarawa attracts $2.3bn investments in seven years — Abdullahi appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Houthi attacks add to worries over Trump Saudi nuclear power pact
items.description: By Patricia Zengerle and Timothy Gardner Nov 20 (Reuters) - Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure are adding to concerns about US President Donald Trump's proposed nuclear power pact with the kingdom, weeks before US senators are due to vote on whether to block the agreement. Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis have intensified drone and missile strikes on Saudi airports, oil facilities and office buildings, raising questions about Riyadh's ability to secure nuclear plants that would be built under the pact.
