And therefore we lose some leverage over China because they’re no longer dependent on American chips? I also think this was wrong, and we thought it was wrong at the time. The reason why is that China knew the importance of advanced chips. As far back as 2014, when America was off fighting ISIS, China recognized, up to the Xi Jinping level and the State Council of China, recognized how important chipmaking was. China at the time was spending more money importing chips than it was spending importing oil. And they couldn’t make any advanced chips at home. So Xi Jinping began an effort when you count the public and private capital upwards of $200 billion to build a chipmaking industry in China. So they had the pedal to the metal on indigenization before we ever took any action. The Trump administration, in their first term, made it a little bit harder. They cut China off the top end of equipment called EV machines—from the company I mentioned before, ASML. And then when we took the controls, we put the controls in place in 2022 on chips. We also put controls in place on chipmaking equipment, another generation of chipmaking equipment, which were imperfect, but what held China back. So the bottom line is even today, even despite the controls and despite China’s more than a decade-long effort to indigenize, chipmaking is so hard that China has failed. And don’t take my word for it: [Commerce Secretary Howard] Lutnick, one of the men at the center of this recent export-control story, testified in 2025 China can make just 200,000 chips. And together, 200,000 for the whole country is not nearly enough. It’s not even enough for a single data center. So those were Nvidia’s arguments, and what our responses were to them. So the policy in 2022, and then some tightenings thereafter, was to say to companies like Nvidia: You may not sell your product; these advanced chips. But it does seem like Megaspeed is an exemplar of two categories of risk that worried us quite a bit when it comes to China’s access to chips. The first is that the chips themselves would be smuggled into China. So they would be purchased in a place like Malaysia or Singapore. There might be some facade of a buyer, potentially a company like Megaspeed in one of those places, that is taking the chips into their data center; is saying, Yes, we’re going to run them here. Everything is good. Don’t worry. And then they’re taking the chips out of the data center, and they’re shipping them into China. And they’re ending up in a Chinese-military data center or the data center of a company that works for the Chinese military, or something like that. And that obviously is a very significant concern for the United States, because that’s direct smuggling of the chips themselves. And we don’t know—once they go into China, we don’t know what the chips are going to be used for. The second category of concern is what’s called remote access. The chips still go to a kind of shady company in Malaysia or Singapore, or a place like that. They go into a data center, but they stay there. The difference is China—Chinese military, Chinese companies—just access that data center remotely over the internet. So the chips stay there, but China can train their next-frontier AI system on this data center, remote. So it’s a different way of circumvent export controls. And we made a decision in one of the export-control updates to try to block that. To say: As a condition of taking these chips, you have to pledge that you will not use them to enable Chinese AI training. President Trump, when he came into office, declined to enforce that rule. So there’s at least a legal gray space—of maybe it was permitted, or the administration wasn’t enforcing it. But those are the two big categories of concern: the actual physical smuggling of the chip, and then the remote access. It’s worth saying Nvidia spent a great deal of time in 2025 and 2026, including Jensen personally, saying chip smuggling is not an issue. And I think it’s obviously incorrect. Warzel: In terms of that remote access to those data centers that are outside of China, for training purposes, it’s known that China has distilled—or sort of reverse-engineered, you know—U.S. models in order to kind of keep up in the race here. Is that where that is happening in your mind? Like, inside those places? Or is that happening more locally? Or is it a mix of the two? Buchanan: Assume it’s a mix. So let’s just be very precise about what’s happening. Distillation is a process in which you can essentially—you know, if folks here are Formula 1 fans, you can draft behind the car in front of you. And you can get the outputs of a leading AI system and come up with the facsimile of that system, imperfectly. You’ll lag capabilities, but it’s cheaper. That is a general concern. And one of the ways in which China has been trying to compensate for the lack of computing power. Essentially, is copying the Americans’ homework. That process of distillation still requires some computing power. And I would imagine China is using whatever computing power it has available to do the process of distillation, whether that’s chips overseas or chips in China. Companies have gotten much better at stopping distillation. So Anthropic, a company that I advise, but I don’t speak for, reported that they came up with methods in the summer of 2026 to stop distillation. I think it was like up to like 99 percent. And I think OpenAI is making some moves in that direction as well. So my suspicion, hard to know for sure, is that we will look at this kind of adversarial distillation as an artifact of a period from 2025 to 2026 where China really struggled with access to computing power, in part due to the export controls, and was using distillation as a way to try to keep up with the frontier. President Trump himself—in, you know, militaristic terms that I would not use, given our discussion before about how we hope to have a positive-sum outcome here—President Trump is very fond of saying: Whoever wins AI, wins . You would think if that is your policy, you would not want to sell chips to China. I don’t get it. I think it’s incoherent for the reason you describe. To be clear about what I do believe, my view is: American companies in fact do have to slow down. And I support pacing the frontier. We haven’t talked about it, but you know, part two of the book is all about how we regulated the AI companies, and what more we need to do on the regulation side. That was sort of huge part of our policy. And my view is that, in fact, the way in which we can create the space for regulation—as far back as 2021, we believed—was to slow China down. And China’s absolute dependence on American computing power was a way for us to slow China down, to build a lead for the United States. And then to, if you’d like, spend that lead on safety, to when the technology got to a critical moment. Which is what we’re in right now. To regulate the companies pretty aggressively, if I had my way. To make sure this technology is safe before it’s rolled out. Without this argument of: Well, we’re in an arms race with China; we must forge ahead . Which I thought was just very destructive. Warzel: So where does this all leave us right now, as we’re sitting in the story here? We’re talking Wednesday, November 18th. Obviously, things are changing by the minute. Buchanan: Always good to timestamp these conversations, ’cause it’s been changing every 24 hours. Warzel: Genuinely, it is. How much hot water is Jensen in? How dangerous and serious is this for Nvidia, as Huang goes to testify before Congress in December? Like, what are the stakes for both Huang and Nvidia going forward? Buchanan: I think they’re very high. Congress, in a bipartisan way, said it’s gonna do an investigation here. I don’t know what’s gonna turn up, but certainly they’ve got a lot of threads to pull. Whether or not there’s a criminal investigation, I have no idea. But I do suspect there will be a lot of government investigations into what happened here, and there should be. I guess in the medium term, Nvidia’s chips are still gonna be really good, and there’s still gonna be big demand for them. So as long as Nvidia can keep making great products, I think they will continue to sell those products. I guess it’s an open question of: Can they make great products without Jensen? We’ll see. They’ve got 31,000 research engineers, or something like that. So there’s a lot of smart people there, and they’ve got a lot of great technology. So we’ll see what happens to them technologically. But yeah; in the context of the investigations, certainly I would describe this as a serious moment. Warzel: What should senators be asking? Or what should anyone in Congress be asking Huang when he’s up there, you know, in front of Congress? Buchanan: It’s the most important, age-old question in any kind of D.C. investigation, which is: What did you know, and when did you know it? And they should be asking Jensen that, and they should be asking the commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick, that. Who knew what about where these chips were going. Who was getting them. How active was Nvidia’s role in enabling smuggling? How active was Jensen’s role? Again, I don’t have firsthand knowledge of the answers. But those were all the questions I’d be asking. Warzel: And I think lastly here, what has this done for the AI ecosystem right now? Like, is it in a worse place than it was? Or let’s just say, the American AI ecosystem? Is it in a worse place than it was two weeks ago, before all of this stuff really trickled out into the press? Or it was about the same? Buchanan: I think it probably creates some turbulence in the waters, but my suspicion is we’ll look back at this in six or 12 months, and the big story of AI will be largely unchanged by this. And the big story of AI, you know—as we spent a lot of detail on the book—is: You have really powerful chips being used by really capable algorithms, at larger and larger scales. Yielding extraordinarily capable systems, with profound national-security implications and profound implications for everyday life and democratic values. That story. To be clear, I’m not a cheerleader for that story. You know, you don’t write a book called The Bitter Struggle if you’re a cheerleader. But I think that story is largely undiminished by these events here. Warzel: What about China? Where are they better off? Are they worse off than they were? Buchanan: They’re worse off. They’re absolutely worse off. Because there was a bipartisan consensus that was forming on denying China access to computing power. But they had big allies that were saying, You know, let’s sell China the chips . And those allies were having some success. Chief amongst some, Jensen. David Sacks, Trump’s—my successor, as you know—AI adviser to the president, was advocating for this, at least based on the reporting. President Trump had advocated for in some context. And now the bipartisan consensus has, at least so far, started to harden against them. That is bad for China’s access to compute, and ultimately that is bad for China. Warzel: Ben Buchanan: Thank you for coming and helping to demystify this; talking about it in these very plain terms. I wanna have you back on, to talk about the regulation part of this, later. But this has been very helpful. Buchanan: It is great to talk about this subject, and it’s great to have interest in this subject of the chips and chip controls. Because this is a wonky subject for sure—that now has gotten this gloss of a sex scandal and a spy story. But I don’t think it’s an exaggeration to say this is one of the most important subjects in the world for U.S. national policy. Warzel: And we’ll keep following it. Thank you very much, Ben, for coming on. Buchanan: Thanks for having me. [ Music ] Warzel: If you liked what you saw here, new episodes of Galaxy Brain drop every Friday. You can subscribe on The Atlantic ’s YouTube channel, or on Apple or Spotify, or wherever it is that you get your podcasts. And if you want to support this work, and the work of my fellow colleagues, you can subscribe to the publication at TheAtlantic.com/Listener. That’s TheAtlantic.com/Listener. Thanks so much, and I’ll see you on the internet. This episode of Galaxy Brain was produced by Hadley Robinson, with story editing by Dave Shaw; the video was edited by Alisa Selman; and the audio was engineered by Rob Smierciak. items.title: Coupe du monde U17 : le Maroc écrase les Fidji
items.description: Les Lionceaux de l’Atlas ont signé une belle entame de leur participation à la Coupe du monde U17 Qatar-2026, en s’imposant face aux Îles Fidji sur le score de 6 buts à 0, en match de la 1ère journée du groupe H, disputé vendredi au terrain N°7 de l’Aspire Zone à Doha. Dès l’entame de la rencontre, les Lionceaux de l’Atlas ont déroulé un jeu offensif qui a fait ses preuves dès la 3e minute du jeu grâce à une ouverture de score de Ismail El Aoud. Toujours dans une dynamique offensive, Ibrahim Rabbaj a accentué l’écart à la 5e minute après une passe lumineuse de Ismail El Aoud. Ziyad Baha a manqué de peu son occasion pour alourdir le résultat (8e), ainsi que son coéquipier Nassim Laarej (10e). Les protégés de Ahmed Kantari ont maintenu leur pression sur le compartiment défensif des Fidjiens qui se sont contentés d’éloigner le danger, sans pour autant faire sortir le ballon plus loin que le milieu de terrain. Très dynamiques dans la surface de réparation adverse, les Lionceaux de l’Atlas sont parvenus à inscrire une troisième réalisation par le biais de Imran Talai (42e) après une passe décisive de Ibrahim Rabbaj. De retour des vestiaires, Ziyad Baha a réussi à chasser son mauvais sort de la première période en transformant la passe décisive de Ismail El Aoud en réalisation (49e) et un penalty six minutes plus tard (55e). Malgré un bloc défensif bas mis en place par les Fidjiens, les Lionceaux de l’Atlas ont réussi à mettre en place leur jeu marqué par une discipline tactique irréprochable et une animation offensive qui a fait la différence au tableau de score, notamment par le biais de Adam Souidi (77e) et Mohamed Obakrim (81e). Rami Lougmani a scellé le sort du match à la 85e minute de jeu, offrant aux Lionceaux de l’Atlas une belle victoire pour leur entrée en lice au Mondial U17. Dans l’autre match de ce groupe, disputé plus tôt sur le terrain N° 5, l’Espagne a dominé la Chine par 5 buts à 0. A l’issue de la première journée du groupe H, le Maroc est en tête avec 3 unités, suivi de l’Espagne (3 pts), des Îles Fidji et du Vietnam qui ferment la marche (0 pt). La prochaine sortie du Maroc en cette compétition l'opposera à la Chine, lundi prochain sur la pelouse du terrain N°2 de l’Aspire Zone. The post Coupe du monde U17 : le Maroc écrase les Fidji appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Indian man sentenced to 19-plus years in plot to assassinate US-based Sikh separatist leader
items.description: A federal judge sentenced an Indian man to 235 months, more than 19 years,in an attempted plot to kill a leading Sikh political figure in the US. Nikhil Gupta, an Indian national, pleaded guilty to murder-for-hire, conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire, and conspiracy to commit money laundering in February. On Friday, the judge said he likely will be deported or removed after his sentence. US prosecutors alleged Gupta was directed by an Indian government official to kill Gurpatwant Singh Pannun, a leading figure of the Khalistan movement, which advocates for an independent homeland for Sikhs. India has denied involvement. Its government has accused Pannun of being a terrorist, which he denies. Pannun, an American citizen, previously told the BBC, “Nikhil Gupta’s guilty plea was judicial confirmation that India’s Modi government orchestrated a structured murder-for-hire assassination plot on American soil”. India has opposed the Khalistan movement, and its political parties also remain opposed to the matter. Sikhs are a religious minority that make up about 2% of India’s population. Some groups have long called for a separate homeland for Sikhs. Prosecutors alleged that in May 2023, Gupta was recruited by Vikash Yadav, an Indian intelligence officer, to carry out an assassination of Pannun. Yadav allegedly provided Gupta with personal information about Pannun, including his address in New York and information about his daily activities, prosecutors said. At his handler’s direction, Gupta contacted someone to facilitate the assassination, but that person was actually a US government informant, prosecutors said. The informant introduced Gupta to a “hitman”, who was actually an undercover officer with the Drug Enforcement Agency. Gupta was arrested in June 2023 at an airport in Prague, Czech Republic and extradited to the US. He has been held at a jail in New York pending his sentencing Friday at a Manhattan court. “He thought that from outside this country he could kill someone in it without consequence, simply for exercising their American right to free speech,” then-US attorney Jay Clayton said in a statement, after announcing Gupta’s guilty plea. Narinder Singh Randhawa, a Sikh separatist and successor of Hardeep Singh Nijjar as temple leader in Surrey, British Columbia, told the BBC the sentencing marks the “first time we see justice” against what he calls historic and systemic persecution of Sikhs by the Indian government in India and abroad. Inderjeet Gosal, another Sikh separatist advocate based in Ontario, called the sentencing “a big community event”. “It’s for all the community to finally witness someone getting caught red-handed.” Gupta’s case placed increased scrutiny on a separate incident, involving the 2023 murder of a Sikh separatist leader in British Columbia, which led to increased tensions between India and Canada. In September 2023, then-Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau said there were “credible allegations potentially linking” India to the murder of Hardeep Singh Nijjar, another advocate for the creation of Khalistan and an associate of Pannun’s. Nijjar was shot and killed by two assailants outside a Sikh temple in British Columbia. India also has denied involvement in his death. The day after Niijar’s murder, US prosecutors allege that Gupta told the undercover officer Nijjar “was also the target” and “we have so many targets.”

items.title: Petrol price reduced by Re1 per litre; diesel increased by Rs2 per litre
items.description: The government on Friday reduced the price of petrol by Re1 per litre while raising that of diesel by Rs2 per litre, after snapping a 12-day streak of consecutive reductions in the rate of petrol the previous day. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs322 per litre and HSD at Rs357 on Nov 21 (Saturday), according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra). Following Tuesday’s reduction of the petrol price to Rs325 per litre, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar highlighted the government’s “proactive measures including policy changes and structural reforms in petroleum policy” that had brought prices back down from their April 3 peak and provided relief through a fuel subsidy scheme. “The government of Pakistan remains committed to continue making all possible efforts to ease the financial burden on the common man amid global challenges,” he said. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. Under an arrangement announced on Nov 2, for 30 days, oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This allows a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end. On Sept 17, the government rolled out the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme across the country to ease the public’s burden amid rising fuel prices due to the Middle East situation. The subsidy scheme applies to owners of motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles of up to 800cc. Rise in fuel prices The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50pc for three months. Since July 17 , the government has been revising fuel prices on a near-daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the conflict. The federal government had also announced targeted relief measures in April to provide subsidised fuel. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.title: Présidentielle en France : Mediapart met un coup de projecteur sur les liens entre Teddy Riner et le roi du Maroc
items.description: Teddy Riner va-t-il payer cher sa photo , torse nu et drape du drapeau francais, en une de l'hebdomadaire Paris-Match ? Dans un article paru le 19 novembre, Mediapart souligne que le cliche – qui fait couler beaucoup d'encre ces derniers jours – a ete pris au Maroc. Un element de la legende « hautement symbolique », a raille le media en ligne, qui s'est attarde sur les liens entre le triple champion olympique francais et le roi du Maroc, Mohammed VI. Selon cette source, Teddy Riner serait en effet le principal actionnaire – a hauteur de 50 % – d'une societe de transport en voiture de luxe, Pullman Limousine, qui exploite une partie du parc automobile d'une societe cette fois-ci integralement detenue par l'athlete : Pullman Rent. Deterrant une note d'une commissaire aux comptes, datant de septembre 2023, Mediapart rapporte ainsi que « la clientele de Pullman Limousine Services » est « composee a 90 % par la delegation du roi du Maroc ». Une societe qui, selon la meme source, a realise entre 2019 et 2022 la bagatelle de 8,7 millions d'euros de chiffre d'affaires et reverse 1,6 million d'euros a Pullman Rent. Des sommes en grande partie concentrees sur la seule annee 2022, a hauteur de 7,1 millions d'euros de chiffre d'affaires, ou le souverain du royaume cherifien a sejourne pres de quatre mois en France. Redresse pour « avantages occultes » Une activite professionnelle qui a par ailleurs valu a Teddy Riner des deboires avec le Fisc, ce dernier accusant le judoka d'etre le « conducteur exclusif » de deux vehicules de sa societe de location, vehicules dont les charges imputees a sa societe « ont constitue des remunerations et avantages occultes pour Teddy Riner » a hauteur de 289 000 euros. Ainsi dans le collimateur de la DGFiP depuis 2019, au titre des exercices 2016 et 2017, l'athlete et entrepreneur a perdu mi-octobre en justice devant la cour administrative d'appel de Versailles qui a conforte l'administration fiscale et souligne une « intention deliberee » de « minorer l'impot ». Par ailleurs, le fraîchement declare candidat a la presidentielle est egalement poursuivi sur ses activites immobilieres , le Fisc lui reclamant pres de 245 000 euros.

items.title: World Children’s Day: Parents must involve children in decisions about their future – Akosua Antwiwah
items.description: A participant in JoyNews’ World Children’s Day celebrations, Akosua Antwiwah, has urged parents to involve their children in decisions that affect their lives, arguing that they should have a say in shaping their own future. She said some parents make decisions on behalf of their children without consulting them or considering their opinions, despite the fact that the children are the ones who will ultimately live with the consequences. Speaking on Joy Prime’s Prime Morning on Friday, November 20, as part of activities marking World Children’s Day, Akosua insisted that children’s rights and views must be respected. “You don’t have any right to take away my right, because it’s for me and not for you,” she said. She expressed concern that children are often excluded from decisions that directly affect their future, stressing that parents must recognise the importance of listening to their aspirations and allowing them to contribute to such choices. “I feel like parents take the decisions of their children for them. They don’t involve the kids in the decisions that they make, forgetting that it’s the child that is going to live their future and not them,” she added. Friday’s broadcasts took an exciting turn as young voices took centre stage across JoyNews and Joy FM, stepping behind the microphones, occupying the news desks and joining studio discussions in a special takeover to mark World Children’s Day 2026. The United Nations Children’s Fund, UNICEF, partnered with JoyNews for this special edition of the World Children’s Day celebration. The young broadcasters brought fresh voices to familiar programmes, trading the classroom for the newsroom and getting a first-hand taste of what it takes to inform, engage and connect with audiences. From the morning shows to the evening news, they joined experienced journalists and presenters to host segments, read bulletins and share their perspectives on issues of national importance. The takeover featured on the AM Show and Prime Morning, where the participants joined discussions on topical issues, offering views shaped by their experiences and concerns about the world around them. They also presented news bulletins during the Midday News on radio and television, taking on the responsibility of delivering information to audiences across the country.

items.title: Sénégal-Maroc U23 : Vieira et Dia appelés à unir leurs forces pour viser la CAN et les JO
items.description: La double confrontation entre le Sénégal et le Maroc, prévue les 22 et 30 mars 2027, dépasse le simple enjeu d'une qualification à la CAN U23 et aux JO de Los Angeles 2028. Entre le contentieux de la dernière CAN senior, les ambitions olympiques et la rivalité sportive entre les deux pays, les Lionceaux joueront bien plus qu'une place en phase finale. Pour franchir cet obstacle, Serigne Saliou Dia devra pouvoir compter sur toutes les forces disponibles. Patrick Vieira est notamment attendu pour faciliter la mise à disposition des jeunes internationaux de l'équipe A éligibles aux U23. Des triomphes sénégalaises en terre marocaine Les Sénégalais ont obtenu leur billet pour le dernier tour en éliminant le Soudan du Sud (0-0 à Juba, 3-1 au retour). Une qualification qui n'a toutefois pas totalement dissipé les interrogations sur le rendement du groupe. Face au Maroc, champion d'Afrique U23 en titre et détenteur du titre mondial chez les U20, le défi sera d'une autre dimension. La CAN U23 prévue en Égypte constitue également le passage obligé vers les Jeux olympiques de Los Angeles 2028, où l'Afrique ambitionne de placer deux représentants. Les finalistes devraient ainsi décrocher les précieux billets olympiques. Mais cette affiche porte aussi le poids d'une histoire récente. Le 18 janvier 2026, à Rabat, le Sénégal avait battu le Maroc (1-0) après prolongation en finale de la CAN senior, grâce à Pape Gueye. Une victoire sur le terrain que le jury d'appel de la CAF a ensuite transformée en succès marocain sur tapis vert, en attribuant un forfait de 3-0 aux Lions. La Fédération sénégalaise de football a saisi le Tribunal arbitral du sport pour contester cette décision. Après l'audience du 8 octobre, le verdict est attendu à la fin du mois de novembre. Les retrouvailles de mars auront donc une saveur particulière. Entre le Maroc et le Sénégal, les retrouvailles n’ont plus rien d’anodin depuis la dernière CAN. Mais s’il est un terrain où les Sénégalais ont de quoi nourrir leur confiance, c’est bien celui du royaume. En juin 2026, les Lionceaux y ont décroché à Rabat leur deuxième titre de champion d’Afrique U17. Quelques mois plus tôt, les Lions avaient eux aussi dominé les Marocains en finale de la CAN senior, une victoire acquise sur la pelouse, même si le TAS doit encore se prononcer sur l’issue de cette rencontre. Le beach soccer vient compléter ce tableau : avec huit couronnes continentales en treize éditions, dont deux conquises sur le sol marocain, en 2011 et 2013, le Sénégal y règne en maître. Autant de preuves que les sélections sénégalaises savent briller chez leur rival. Vieira et Dia, une même ambition Pour éviter de laisser passer cette double opportunité, Serigne Saliou Dia aura besoin d'un groupe étoffé. Le sélectionneur pourrait notamment bénéficier de l'apport de plusieurs jeunes internationaux de l'équipe A. Mamadou Sarr, Mamadou Diakhon, Ibrahima Mbaye, Paul Mendy ou encore le gardien Mamour Ndiaye représentent des profils susceptibles d'apporter de l'expérience et de la qualité aux Lionceaux, sous réserve de leur éligibilité et de leur disponibilité en club. Patrick Vieira aura donc un rôle important à jouer dans cette articulation. La qualification de l'équipe A à la CAN 2027 permet d'envisager une meilleure coordination entre les deux staffs. L'objectif n'est pas de déshabiller une sélection pour renforcer l'autre, mais de construire une stratégie commune autour d'une échéance qui engage l'avenir du football sénégalais en mars 2027. Le Maroc suit déjà cette logique. Selon la presse marocaine, Mohamed Ouahbi est également appelé à faciliter la mise à disposition de plusieurs jeunes talents de l'équipe A au profit de la sélection olympique. Ali Maamar, Ayyoub Bouaddi, Yassir Zabiri, Yassine Gessime et Samir El Mourabit figurent parmi les joueurs évoqués. Abdellah Ouazane, Soufian El Faouzi et Abdelhamid Aït Boudlal constituent d'autres profils susceptibles d'enrichir ce vivier. Le Maroc entend ainsi mobiliser sa jeune génération pour défendre son statut continental et retrouver les Jeux. Ne pas répéter les erreurs de 2023 Le Sénégal connaît pourtant le prix d'une mauvaise coordination entre ses sélections. En mars 2023, les Lionceaux avaient dominé le Mali (3-1) à Diamniadio avant de s'effondrer au retour à Bamako (0-3). Cette élimination les avait privés de la CAN U23 et des Jeux olympiques de Paris 2024. Dion Lopy et Formose Mendy, initialement concernés par le groupe de Demba Mbaye, avaient entre-temps rejoint l'équipe A après leur convocation incomprehensible par Aliou Cissé. Ce précédent doit servir de leçon. Quatre ans plus tard, le Sénégal retrouve une situation où la gestion des effectifs peut peser aussi lourd que les choix tactiques. Le Maroc anticipe déjà la mobilisation de ses jeunes internationaux. La Tanière ne peut se permettre de laisser passer cette opportunité. En mars, les deux sélections auront 180 minutes voire plus pour se départager. Au-delà de la rivalité et du contentieux qui opposent les deux fédérations, les Lionceaux devront surtout répondre présents sur le terrain. Pour atteindre l'Égypte et rêver de Los Angeles, Vieira et Dia devront parler le même langage. Cette fois, l'union des forces ne doit pas rester un slogan : elle doit devenir une stratégie. Par Cheikh Gora DIOP

items.title: Gov’t spent $4.67m on Black Stars’ 2026 World Cup campaign
items.description: Ghana’s Minister of Sports and Recreation, Kofi Adams, says the government spent $4.67m of the $5m advance allocated for the Black Stars’ participation in the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The minister disclosed this while answering questions about his ministry in Parliament, explaining that the expenditure covered players’ appearance fees, payments to the technical team and support staff, honoraria, per diems and operational costs. Per a Facebook post from Parliament official account, Adams said a total of $4,673,337.46 was spent, leaving an unspent balance of $326,662.54. Players received the largest share of the expenditure, with $2.6m paid in appearance fees. Each player received $100,000, while the technical team was paid $1.3m. The minister also disclosed that $390,000 was spent on honoraria, with a further $278,300 allocated to per diems for players and members of the technical team. Other expenses included $19,212.09 in commission charges and $1,393.26 for accommodation. A further $84,432.11 was spent on transportation, medical services, feeding and other incidental expenses. Adams said the figures were consistent with the expenditure report he presented to Parliament’s Committee on Youth and Sports. The disclosure provides a breakdown of how the government’s US$5m advance for Ghana’s World Cup participation was utilised, with approximately 93.5% of the funds spent. Ghana are preparing for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, which will be hosted by the United States, Canada and Mexico.

items.title: Obuasi East ambulance returns to service after five years off the road
items.description: Residents of the Obuasi East Municipality are set to benefit from improved emergency medical transportation after the municipal ambulance was restored to service following a GH¢50,000 donation by the Chief Executive Officer of Obuasi Beverages, Dr Collins Amo. The contribution went towards replacing the vehicle’s faulty engine and repairing it after it had remained off the road for nearly five years. The repaired ambulance was formally presented to Dr Amo by the Obuasi East Municipal Ambulance Director, SAEMT Irene Cynthia Akornor, who thanked him for supporting the restoration. Dr Amo expressed satisfaction with the vehicle’s return to service and called for greater private-sector participation in addressing critical community needs. He said individuals and corporate institutions had a role to play in complementing government efforts to improve healthcare delivery and other essential public services. The Municipal Chief Executive of Obuasi East, William Kofi Adzowu, also expressed appreciation to Dr Amo, describing the intervention as a response to an important healthcare need. He said the prolonged unavailability of the ambulance had created difficulties for emergency medical transportation in the municipality and urged other businesses, corporate institutions and individuals to support initiatives that improve access to essential services. SAEMT Akornor said the restoration would strengthen emergency healthcare delivery, particularly for vulnerable residents. She explained that a functional ambulance was essential for transporting accident victims, critically ill patients and pregnant women who require urgent medical attention. The return of the vehicle is expected to improve the municipality’s capacity to provide emergency medical transportation. Ambulance had been out of service for years The restoration addresses a longstanding operational challenge for the municipality. In 2024, the Obuasi Municipal Assembly disclosed that the Obuasi East ambulance had been out of service for approximately three years following an accident, placing additional pressure on the ambulance serving Obuasi and surrounding communities. The latest intervention by Dr Amo adds to his previous contributions to healthcare and community development in the Obuasi area. In 2024, he donated GH¢200,000 towards the Heal Komfo Anokye Project, which is raising funds to renovate and improve the Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital. In 2025, he also donated locally produced baby diapers to selected health facilities in the Obuasi East and Obuasi West municipalities to support maternity and child-welfare services. The GH¢50,000 contribution has restored an essential emergency response vehicle and highlights the potential role of private-sector support in addressing gaps in public service delivery.

items.title: IET-Ghana inducts 265 engineers, warns against misuse of professional stamps
items.description: The Institution of Engineering and Technology, Ghana (IET-GH), has inducted 265 engineers into the profession, cautioning them against the misuse of professional stamps, which could expose them to legal consequences and liability for unsafe or substandard work. The newly inducted engineers have been urged to scrutinise designs, technical documents and projects thoroughly before certifying them with their professional stamps, as the certification makes them accountable for the quality, accuracy and safety of the work. Speaking at the 40th Annual General Conference and Induction Ceremony, the institution’s President, Engr. Wonder Davor, said the names of the inductees would be forwarded to the Engineering Council for licensing. He said that the engineers could not practice as professional engineers without obtaining the requisite licences. Engr. Davor said the professional stamps presented to the inductees were important tools for their work but warned them against using them indiscriminately. He explained that stamping or certifying a design or technical document meant accepting responsibility for the work and its consequences. “Anything that they stamp or certify with the stamp means that they are taking responsibility upon themselves. Should there be any problem, they will be held responsible,” he said. He urged the engineers to examine all documents and designs presented to them for certification to ensure they met the required standards before approving them. According to him, engineers must not certify work without properly assessing its technical quality and compliance with professional requirements. He said their decisions could have serious consequences for public safety, particularly where faulty designs or substandard construction could result in accidents, injuries or loss of life. Engr. Davor urged the inductees to make public safety their priority and ensure their professional decisions did not expose people to unnecessary risks. “As they go out, they should take it upon themselves to ensure that whatever they do, they consider people’s safety and public safety, and make sure they are not putting the public at risk,” he said. The IET-Ghana President also warned engineers against using expired professional stamps, describing the practice as a violation of the law. He said engineers whose professional registrations or subscriptions had expired were not authorised to certify documents until they had renewed their membership and registration. According to him, practising with an expired stamp effectively means operating without valid professional registration. “Those who are using expired stamps are equally violating the law. It is as if they are not registered professionals because once your service expires, you are not supposed to certify any document again,” he said. He advised engineers to renew their subscriptions with their professional bodies and ensure their licences remained valid before undertaking certification duties. Engr. Davor said maintaining valid registration was essential to ensuring accountability and protecting the integrity of the engineering profession. The induction ceremony formed part of activities marking IET-Ghana’s 40th Annual General Conference, which brought together engineering professionals and stakeholders to discuss professional standards, innovation, technology and the role of engineering in national development.

items.description: Cinq corps sans vie sont déposés à la morgue du CHU de Pala, selon la commune de Bobo-Dioulasso, ce vendredi 20 novembre 2026, dans un communiqué. Communiqué de la commune de Bobo-Dioulasso Cinq (05) corps sans vie déposés à la morgue du CHU de Pala Le Président de la Délégation spéciale de la Commune de Bobo-Dioulasso informe la population que cinq (05) corps sans vie ont été découverts et déposés à la morgue du Centre Hospitalier Universitaire de Pala. Il s’agit de quatre personnes non identifiées et d’une adolescente de 15 ans, identifiée sous le nom de Ouédraogo Salamata. Toute personne susceptible de reconnaître l’un des défunts ou de fournir des informations utiles à leur identification est invitée à se présenter à la morgue du CHU de Pala, munie de tout document ou renseignement utile. La Commune invite les populations à relayer largement cette information afin de faciliter l’identification des défunts et les démarches auprès des familles. items.title: La présidentielle française de 2027 pourrait affaiblir le soutien européen à l’Ukraine et provoquer des divisions au sein de l’UE
items.description: L'election presidentielle francaise de 2027 pourrait entraîner une revision de la politique de Paris envers l'Ukraine et compliquer la poursuite du soutien europeen a Kiev. Dans une enquete publiee le 20 novembre, Politico rapporte les preoccupations de plusieurs responsables europeens et ukrainiens face a la possibilite d'un changement de cap a l'elysee. Le premier tour est prevu le 18 avril 2027 et le second, si necessaire, le 2 mai. Selon les sondages cites dans l'enquete, Marine Le Pen et Jean-Luc Melenchon figurent parmi les candidats susceptibles d'acceder au second tour. Tous deux contestent certains choix d'Emmanuel Macron concernant le conflit ukrainien. Marine Le Pen estime que les difficultes budgetaires francaises ne permettent plus de maintenir l'aide financiere a Kiev. Elle souhaite mettre fin a l'assistance, tout en conservant certaines cooperations militaires, notamment la formation des soldats ukrainiens. Jean-Luc Melenchon s'oppose, quant a lui, aux frappes ukrainiennes en profondeur sur le territoire russe. Il avait aussi evoque un referendum dans le Donbass permettant a ses habitants de se prononcer sur leur avenir. La proposition, critiquee a Kiev, avait ensuite fait l'objet de precisions de sa part. Le soutien europeen et les sanctions contre Moscou en question Pour les responsables interroges, les consequences d'une alternance francaise depasseraient la question du financement de Kiev. Leur principale preoccupation concerne la capacite de l'Union europeenne a maintenir une position commune. La France joue un role important dans la coordination. Elle copreside la « Coalition des volontaires », participe aux discussions sur les garanties de securite et contribue aux positions europeennes sur les negociations de paix. « En matiere de soutien financier, la France n'a jamais figure parmi les dix premiers. Mais concernant le risque de rupture du consensus europeen, ce serait un veritable defi », a declare un responsable ukrainien a Politico. Les avis restent toutefois partages. Sur les huit responsables et diplomates europeens et ukrainiens interroges, environ la moitie redoutent un affaiblissement du soutien a Kiev. Les autres estiment que les candidats pourraient moderer leurs positions une fois au pouvoir. Un eventuel changement a l'elysee pourrait aussi peser sur les sanctions contre Moscou. Selon un diplomate occidental cite par le media, le Rassemblement national chercherait a les assouplir. Leur renouvellement exigeant l'unanimite des etats membres, un veto francais risquerait d'empecher leur prolongation. a ses yeux, la hausse des prix de l'energie raviverait l'interet de certains pays europeens pour le petrole et le gaz russes. Berlin veut preserver le financement de Kiev La perspective d'un changement de politique francaise conduit Berlin a rechercher des mecanismes de financement moins exposes aux blocages. Selon le media, le chancelier allemand, Friedrich Merz, souhaite inscrire l'aide a Kiev dans le prochain budget europeen et permettre que certaines decisions soient prises a la majorite qualifiee plutot qu'a l'unanimite. De son cote, Volodymyr Zelensky tente de relativiser les consequences d'une eventuelle alternance francaise. « Nous travaillerons avec celui ou celle que les Francais eliront », a-t-il declare a Politico. Moscou, pour sa part, considere que la poursuite de l'aide militaire occidentale a l'Ukraine contribue uniquement a prolonger le conflit, une position souvent rappelee par les autorites russes.

Mondial U17 : à dix, le Sénégal sauve un point face à la Croatie
items.description: Un début de Coupe du monde mitigé, mais un point qui pourrait compter. Vendredi à Doha, les Lionceaux de Lamine Sané ont arraché le match nul (1-1) face à la Croatie lors de la première journée du groupe F. Menés dès la 8e minute et privés d'un joueur avant la pause, les champions d'Afrique ont su rester debout. Sur la pelouse du Pitch 2 de l'ASPIRE Academy, le Sénégal rate son entrée. Luka Bartolović, titulaire dans le onze de Budimir, profite d'une action à peine entamée pour ouvrir le score dès la 8e minute. La frappe laisse Baba Camara, préféré à Assane Sarr, sans solution. Après cela, les Sénégalais cherchent leurs marques, mais peinent à se procurer des occasions franches. Pire, le scénario se durcit à la 42e minute, quand Abdou Karim Diallo est expulsé. À dix contre onze, avec un but à remonter, la tâche paraît lourde. Réaction juste avant la pause C'est pourtant là que le Sénégal frappe. Sur un coup de pied arrêté, Sadio sert Sega Fall Mbodji, qui égalise juste avant la mi-temps. Un but précieux, qui renvoie les deux équipes aux vestiaires à égalité. Après la pause, la Croatie pousse mais ne parvient pas à faire la différence. Vers l'heure de jeu, la VAR est consultée sur une action litigieuse dans la surface sénégalaise : pas de penalty. Le Sénégal gère ensuite l'usure à coups de remplacements : Moussa Faye et Pape Guèye entrent à la 73e, Ismaïla Konté à la 87e, puis Fallou Gomis dans les arrêts de jeu à la place de Sadio. En face, Zagreb réagit avec Toni Ruso et Petar Lačić, sans trouver la faille. Ce point lance le tournoi des Lionceaux. Ils retrouveront Cuba lundi, une équipe battue 5-3 par le Tadjikistan pour sa première sortie. Une occasion de décrocher une première victoire. O.B.N

items.title: National Apprenticeship Programme graduates to get priority support from Women’s Development Bank – Mahama
items.description: President John Mahama says women who graduate from the National Apprenticeship Programme and intend to establish their own businesses will receive priority support through the Women’s Development Bank. He says the government will submit the names of interested graduates to the bank when it is launched to facilitate access to appropriate financing and business support. He said, “When the Women’s Development Bank is launched, trainees who want to set up their businesses, we will give your names to the bank, and they will give you priority support”. Speaking at the graduation ceremony of the programme’s maiden cohort in Accra, President Mahama also announced plans to connect beneficiaries to employment opportunities through labour mobility agreements with other countries and companies participating in the 24-hour economy. He disclosed that Ghana has received requests from countries in the Caribbean and the Middle East for skilled workers to be engaged on fixed-term contracts. He mentioned welders, steel vendors and other skilled workers as potential beneficiaries, explaining that the government would use the programme’s database to identify workers whose skills match the requirements of prospective employers. He said, “Opportunities also exist through the labour mobility agreements that we are signing with other countries. We have received requests from countries in the Caribbean and the Middle East to send skilled workers on fixed-term contracts. “Skilled workers like steel vendors, welders, and so when those requests come, we will look into your database and find the skills that they are looking for, and then we will ship you abroad to go and work on a fixed-term contract” President Mahama said the government would also provide companies registered under the 24-hour economy policy with the database of trained beneficiaries and encourage them to prioritise their recruitment. He further called on businesses, contractors and public institutions to provide work opportunities for the graduates, mentor young artisans and engage them as suppliers where they meet the required standards. The President said the Adwumawura programme would support graduates interested in establishing their own businesses, while the One Million Coders Programme could provide further digital training relevant to their areas of work. He added that companies established under the New Economy Programme, which involves a planned investment of 10 billion dollars over four years, would be encouraged to employ graduates of the National Apprenticeship Programme. He cited opportunities in the textiles and garments sector, where companies could employ beneficiaries trained in tailoring and dressmaking.

items.title: GRNMA Ashanti warns against brain drain, holds youth boot camp to improve livelihoods of nurses
items.description: Ashanti Regional Chairman of the Ghana Registered Nurses and Midwives Association (GRNMA), Jones Afriyie-Anto, has raised concerns over the significant brain drain associated with the Ghana Labour Exchange Programme (GLEP). Speaking on the sidelines of the maiden edition of the GRNMA Youth Boot Camp at Ejisu-Krapa, Afriyie-Anto lamented that an initiative meant for jobless nurses and midwives is instead targeting experienced specialists who constitute the backbone of Ghana’s health system for foreign employment. He explained that the Association does not oppose the migration of health workers, particularly in light of the large number of unemployed trained nurses and midwives, but it is concerned about the calibre of personnel being targeted for recruitment. “We approve of the migration of health workers to other countries, especially when Ghana has a backlog of nurses and midwives who completed their courses since 2021 and are still at home up to 2025. In fact, we will support government to do that,” he said. The GLEP is a government-led initiative connecting Ghanaian health workers and other professionals with legal, structured international job opportunities. Mr. Anto Afriyie said recruiting unemployed graduates would not only reduce unemployment among nurses and midwives, but also protect the already strained health system from collapse. “What we are against is the personnel the foreign countries are coming for. For instance, when they come, they want the emergency nurse specialists, the oncology nurses, the specialised nurses, the Deputy Chief Nursing Officers, Principal Nursing Officers who have the experience and are the backbone, the anchors of the health system in Ghana. Those are the people they are recruiting,” he stated. Mr. Afriyie-Anto warned that losing such experienced officers would weaken healthcare delivery in Ghana, particularly in critical areas like emergency and cancer care. “That is going to bring down our health system. What we want them to recruit is those who have completed school and are in the house. Let them recruit those people so that the unemployment rate will go down. Not those who are already employed and are doing well in the country and are the anchors of the health system,” he added. The Ashanti Regional Chairman of the GRNMA, therefore, urged the government to urgently review the migration policy to ensure that it prioritises unemployed nurses and midwives instead of depleting the country of its experienced specialists. In a bid to enhance the skills and retain the expertise of both employed and unemployed nursing and midwifery professionals in the Ashanti region, the GRNMA organised a Youth Boot camp to build their capacity in leadership, mentorship, professional conduct and skills development in batik making. The programme, themed “Shaping the Future: Youth Voices in Nursing and Midwifery,” was also held to commemorate International Youth Day. Delivering the keynote address, Nelly Desiadenyo Goka, the President of the Association of Human Resource Management Practitioners in Health Ghana (AHRMPGH), Ashanti Chapter, urged young nurses and midwives to embrace leadership, mentor one another and uphold professionalism in their practice. She stressed the importance of mentorship, noting that without deliberate grooming of young professionals, the health system would face a serious leadership gap. “We should also be able to mentor each other, especially the elderly ones, the seniors amongst us. They should be able to mentor the young ones so that in their absence, the young ones can take over. If not, there will be a very big gap which we will not be able to cover,” she stated. According to her, the time has come for the youth to prepare themselves to take over from the older generation, who will soon exit the healthcare system. She also challenged young women in the profession to be bold and step forward for leadership, pointing out that nursing and midwifery is female-dominated. Touching on professionalism, she urged the young professionals to be meticulous in discharging their duties and not use working hours for social media leisure. “We usually acquire knowledge when we go online and all that. We can do that outside work. We can do that in our free time, but not when we are working, attending to patients. Imagine if the same thing is done to you, or your mother calls you to tell you that, ‘I went to the hospital and this is how I’ve been treated by a nurse or midwife.’ We may not like it,” she said. In addition to leadership and mentorship, participants were engaged in professional hands-on skills training in batik, also known as tie and dye. The Middle Zone Coordinator of the Youth Boot Camp, Philemon Adu Brempong, revealed that the skills training was deliberately included to give participants something practical they could fall back on, whether they were already working or still waiting to be posted. Mr. Adu Brempong also highlighted the plight of unemployed nurses who have stayed home for years awaiting postings from government, stressing that nurses cannot rely on one income stream, especially those with children. “For those who are yet to start work, they do not have any source of finance. And this also acts as an opportunity for them to do something for themselves as they sit home and await postings from government,” he said.

items.title: Deepfake : des vidéos de plus en plus difficiles à démasquer
items.description: Des videos truquees mettant en scene des personnalites publiques circulent de plus en plus sur les reseaux sociaux. Elles sont parfois si realistes qu'il devient difficile de distinguer le vrai du faux. Des sequences mettant en scene des joueurs de football, des personnalites publiques ou d'autres personnes connues circulent regulierement sur les reseaux sociaux. Certaines sont tellement convaincantes qu'il devient difficile de soupconner une manipulation. Ces contenus, appeles deepfakes , sont realises a l'aide de technologies d'intelligence artificielle capables de modifier ou de generer des images et des voix. Des outils d'IA rendent les manipulations plus realistes Des outils comme Veo, DeepSwap ou FaceFusion facilitent la creation de videos truquees. Ils permettent notamment de generer des sequences, de remplacer un visage ou de reproduire certains mouvements et expressions. Avec les progres de ces technologies, les anomalies autrefois relativement faciles a reperer deviennent moins evidentes. Un decalage entre les mouvements des levres et la voix, des gestes incoherents ou des mouvements de mains peu naturels pouvaient autrefois eveiller les soupcons. Aujourd'hui, ces indices ne suffisent plus toujours a identifier une video manipulee. La qualite visuelle d'une sequence ne constitue donc plus une garantie d'authenticite. Une video nette, avec des mouvements fluides et des expressions naturelles, peut-elle aussi avoir ete generee ou modifiee par l'intelligence artificielle. Des outils de detection utiles, mais pas infaillibles Pour analyser une video suspecte, certains outils en ligne peuvent apporter une premiere indication. C'est notamment le cas de Hive Moderation et de Deepware Scanner, qui proposent des analyses destinees a reperer d'eventuelles manipulations. Cependant, leurs resultats doivent etre interpretes avec prudence. Ces outils peuvent passer a cote de certaines videos truquees ou signaler a tort un contenu authentique. Aucun resultat ne suffit donc, a lui seul, a confirmer qu'une video est vraie ou fausse. Cinq reflexes a adopter face a une video suspecte En l'absence de certitude, la verification de la source reste essentielle. Avant de partager une video, plusieurs reflexes peuvent aider a eviter les pieges. Rechercher l'origine de la video, verifier le contexte, rechercher d'autres sources, analyser les images et le son, utiliser les outils de detection avec prudence. Face a la sophistication croissante des deepfakes, la vigilance reste indispensable. Une video peut sembler parfaitement reelle sans l'etre. Avant de croire ou de partager, il faut toujours verifier. items.title: MTN Ghana marks 30 years of operations, acknowledges customers and stakeholders
items.description: MTN Ghana has marked 30 years of operations in the country, acknowledging the contribution of customers, employees, business partners, government institutions and communities to its growth. The company is celebrating the milestone under the theme, “30 Years of Progress, Powered by You,” which it says reflects its contribution to expanding connectivity and supporting Ghana’s digital and socio-economic development. In a statement issued on November 17, 2026, MTN Ghana said its growth over the past three decades had been driven by the trust and support of individuals and institutions across the country. Since commencing operations in Ghana, the telecommunications company has expanded access to communication and financial services, connecting individuals, businesses and communities. It has also invested in digital skills development, innovation and community initiatives, particularly in education, healthcare, youth empowerment, entrepreneurship and financial inclusion through the MTN Ghana Foundation and other sustainability programmes. Chief Executive Officer of MTN Ghana, Stephen Blewett, said the company’s relationships with customers and stakeholders remained central to its achievements. He said the anniversary was an opportunity to recognise those who had contributed to the company’s development over the years. “This milestone belongs to every customer who has chosen MTN, every community that has welcomed us, every employee who has served with dedication, and every stakeholder who has partnered with us over the years,” he said. MTN Ghana also acknowledged the contributions of government, regulatory bodies, traditional authorities, business partners, shareholders, the media, civil society organisations and local communities to its operations. The company said its growth was closely linked to the development of the communities in which it operates, a commitment it intends to maintain through its investments and partnerships. Looking ahead, MTN Ghana said it would continue to strengthen stakeholder relationships, expand digital inclusion and introduce innovative solutions to support individuals, businesses and communities. The anniversary marks 30 years of operations for Scancom PLC, the company behind MTN Ghana. It is listed on the Ghana Stock Exchange and is part of the MTN Group, which operates across emerging markets.

items.title: Kumasi Central Prison holds 1,600 inmates against 500 capacity as authorities intensify decongestion
items.description: The Kumasi Central Prison is holding an average of 1,600 inmates, more than three times its authorised capacity of 500, as the Ashanti Regional Prisons Command steps up efforts to ease overcrowding. The facility, built in 1901, is among the prisons facing pressure from rising inmate numbers, with remand prisoners identified as a major contributor to the congestion. The regional command is pursuing a multi-pronged decongestion strategy involving inmate transfers, closer coordination with the police and judiciary, and interventions under the Justice for All Programme. Chief Superintendent Richard Bukari, the Ashanti Regional Prisons Service Public Relations Officer, said the command regularly transfers eligible inmates to camp prisons to reduce pressure on congested facilities. He cited the Ejura Camp Prison, built by the Church of Pentecost, as one of the facilities receiving inmates from Kumasi. “From time to time, we do a transfer of the least harmful inmates to some of our camp prisons. A typical example is Ejura Camp Prison, which is a state-of-the-art prison built for us by the Church of Pentecost, which we appreciate so much,” he said. Mr Bukari said about 150 inmates had been earmarked for transfer to Ejura as part of the latest decongestion effort. “Even only today, there was some transfer of about 150 earmarked for Ejura. And can you imagine 150 taken out? At least it will help decongest the facility,” he added. Mr Bukari explained that transfers to camp prisons were not automatic and depended on legal and security considerations, including the length of an inmate’s sentence, the nature of the offence and rehabilitation progress. He said camp prisons operated with lower security requirements and were therefore intended for inmates considered suitable for such placements. “It is ultra-modern, a state-of-the-art prison facility, but by law or legally, not every inmate qualifies to be there, on basis of number of years being number of years you are serving, and the calibre of crime or the type of crime that brought you to the prison,” he said. He added that some inmates had personally requested transfers to Ejura, but such applications had to be assessed against the applicable requirements. “It is a camp prison; its security standards aren’t so high, and every inmate qualified to be there is one who is not a threat in whatever way to the public,” he said. Beyond inmate transfers, the Ashanti Regional Prisons Command is working to address delays in the justice delivery process, particularly cases in which police investigators fail to attend court with remand prisoners. Mr Bukari said the Regional Prisons Commander, Deputy Director of Prisons James Mwinyelle, was concerned about investigators who failed to collect inmates for scheduled court appearances. He said the command had taken steps to follow up with investigators and ensure that inmates were presented before the courts when their cases were due. According to him, the intervention could help eligible remand prisoners secure bail and leave custody. The command is also relying on periodic court sittings under the Justice for All Programme to review cases involving inmates. Under the programme, courts sit within prison facilities to hear qualifying cases, allowing some matters to be resolved without requiring inmates to be transported to regular court premises. Mr Bukari said the process had resulted in some cases being dismissed or inmates being discharged, helping to reduce the prison population. The Prisons Service’s paralegal department is also supporting efforts to identify cases that qualify for legal intervention. The regional command says the combined measures are intended to ease congestion while ensuring that inmate transfers and other interventions comply with legal and security requirements.

items.title: Crises des routes maritimes et vulnérabilité énergétique de l’Afrique : l’intégration régionale comme réponse stratégique (Dr Kemoko DIAKITÉ)
items.description: Les crises des routes maritimes du détroit d’Ormuz et de Bab el- Mandeb posent des défis sur la vulnérabilité énergétique en Afrique. Quelles réponses devra apporter l’Afrique dans le cadre de l’intégration régionale ? I. Ormuz et Bab el-Mandeb : les fragilités des approvisionnements mondiaux Le détroit d’Ormuz est un passage maritime stratégique situé au Moyen-Orient, entre l’Iran et Oman. Reliant le golfe Persique au golfe d’Oman puis à l’océan Indien, il constitue l’un des principaux points de passage du commerce énergétique international. Selon l’Agence internationale de l’énergie (AIE), près de 20 millions de barils de pétrole brut et de produits pétroliers par jour ont transité par le détroit d’Ormuz en 2025, soit environ un quart du commerce pétrolier maritime mondial. Ce passage est également essentiel pour les exportations de gaz naturel liquéfié (GNL) du Qatar et des Émirats arabes unis, représentant près d’un cinquième du commerce mondial de GNL. La dépendance à ce corridor concerne notamment l’Arabie saoudite, l’Irak, le Koweït, le Qatar, Bahreïn et les Émirats arabes unis. Les affrontements de 2026 impliquant notamment les États-Unis, Israël et l’Iran ont accentué l’insécurité dans cette zone et provoqué de fortes perturbations de la circulation maritime, sans qu’il soit rigoureux de parler d’une fermeture totale et permanente. Les risques d’attaques, les restrictions de navigation, la hausse des primes d’assurance et les détournements d’itinéraires ont affecté les coûts et les délais d’approvisionnement. Les tensions sur les marchés du pétrole et du gaz se répercutent sur les prix des carburants, du transport, de l’électricité et des denrées, et peuvent alourdir sensiblement les dépenses de soutien public à l’énergie. A titre d’exemple le Qatar est très affecté car ayant perdu 24 milliards de dollars en six mois. Ormuz est le principal détroit par où passent les tankers qataris. En outre, selon le FMI, le PIB de l'Arabie Saoudite, un des plus grands producteurs de pétrole devrait se contracter de 3, 3 %, soit cinq points de moins selon les prévisions. Le conflit entre l'Iran qui a verrouillé le détroit d’Ormuz et ciblé les alliés de Washington dans le Golfe et les États Unis d'Amérique a causé environ 200 milliards de dollars us de dégâts matériels dans les pays du Conseil de coopération du Golfe (Arabie saoudite, Oman, Qatar, Bahreïn, Émirats arabes Unis et Koweït) selon un rapport d'Allianz Trade publié le 10 novembre 2026. Il a également eu des répercussions négatives sur le tourisme et l'immobilier dans cette zone. Le détroit de Bab el-Mandeb, situé entre le Yémen, Djibouti et l’Érythrée, relie le golfe d’Aden à la mer Rouge et, par le canal de Suez, à la Méditerranée. Il constitue une autre artère essentielle des échanges entre l’Asie, l’Afrique et l’Europe. Les attaques et menaces exercées par les Houthis contre la navigation commerciale dans la mer Rouge, ainsi que leur présence sur une partie du littoral yéménite, ont contribué à accroître les risques dans ce corridor. En 2026, des menaces ciblées visant notamment certains navires liés à l’Arabie saoudite ont été signalées. Il importe cependant de distinguer cette capacité d’entrave d’un contrôle intégral du détroit. Le recours à des routes de contournement, notamment autour du cap de Bonne-Espérance, peut allonger les voyages, mobiliser davantage de navires et renchérir le fret. Ces crises rappellent que la sécurité énergétique des États africains ne dépend pas uniquement de leurs ressources nationales : elle est aussi tributaire de la sûreté des voies maritimes, de la solidité des chaînes logistiques et de la capacité des économies à absorber les chocs extérieurs. II. Le paradoxe énergétique africain et ses conséquences économiques L’Afrique possède un potentiel énergétique immense mais fait face à de forts contrastes en matière d’accès et d’infrastructures. Selon l’AIE, environ 600 millions de personnes en Afrique subsaharienne, soit près de 47 % de la population de cette région en 2024, n’avaient toujours pas accès à l’électricité. L’initiative Mission 300, portée par la Banque mondiale et la Banque africaine de développement, vise à raccorder 300 millions de personnes à l’électricité à l’horizon 2030. Cette réalité révèle un paradoxe : bien que dotée de ressources abondantes en pétrole, gaz, hydroélectricité, solaire et éolien, l’Afrique demeure, dans plusieurs de ses régions, dépendante d’importations de produits raffinés, d’équipements et de services énergétiques. La production de pétrole brut ne garantit pas à elle seule la disponibilité de carburants, pas davantage que l’existence de centrales électriques ne garantit la continuité de l’approvisionnement en combustible. Les impacts des crises internationales varient selon les pays : les importateurs nets supportent des pressions sur les balances commerciales et les devises ; certains États producteurs restent exposés faute de capacités suffisantes de raffinage ; les pays enclavés subissent des coûts logistiques plus élevés. Dans tous les cas, l’inflation, les subventions énergétiques et la compétitivité industrielle peuvent être affectées. La sécurité énergétique devient ainsi un enjeu de souveraineté budgétaire, de stabilité sociale et de développement économique. III. Quelles réponses pour l’Afrique ? Face à ces risques, les pays africains ne sauraient se limiter à des réponses conjoncturelles. Ils doivent inscrire la sécurité d’approvisionnement dans des politiques énergétiques de long terme, articulant investissements nationaux, intégration régionale et coopération internationale. Plusieurs priorités complémentaires se dégagent. 1. Faire de l’énergie une priorité de politique publique et renforcer les capacités nationales de production, de transformation et de stockage. Les sociétés nationales, aux côtés d’investisseurs privés soumis à une régulation adaptée, doivent jouer un rôle structurant. Le raffinage constitue à cet égard un levier important de résilience. Il convient de saluer le protocole d’accord signé le 23 septembre 2026, à New York, entre la Société africaine de raffinage (SAR) du Sénégal et le groupe turc Yamata, en vue de la construction d’une deuxième raffinerie d’environ 4 millions de tonnes par an, pour un investissement envisagé de 2 à 3 milliards de dollars, et de la modernisation de la raffinerie existante. La réalisation de ces ambitions devra toutefois reposer sur des financements sécurisés, la compétitivité des installations et l’existence de débouchés nationaux et régionaux. 2. Accélérer l’intégration énergétique régionale. Les organisations sous-régionales doivent mutualiser leurs moyens pour développer les infrastructures de production et de transport ainsi que les échanges transfrontaliers d’électricité. Le Système d’échanges d’énergie électrique ouest-africain (WAPP/EEEOA), créé par décision de la CEDEAO en 1999, doit être renforcé comme instrument de développement d’un marché régional fiable et compétitif. À l’échelle continentale, le Marché africain unique de l’électricité (AfSEM), porté par l’Union africaine, offre une perspective de convergence réglementaire, d’interconnexions et d’investissements coordonnés. Il convient de passer d’une logique de projets juxtaposés à une planification énergétique véritablement régionale. 3. Développer un mix énergétique diversifié, incluant, là où les conditions sont réunies, le nucléaire civil. L’Afrique du Sud exploite de longue date la centrale nucléaire de Koeberg, tandis que l’Égypte construit celle d’El-Dabaa. D’autres pays, dont le Ghana, le Maroc et le Rwanda, poursuivent à des degrés divers des travaux préparatoires. Le Sénégal s’est également engagé dans la préparation structurée d’un programme électronucléaire civil ; l’atelier national de septembre 2026 consacré au dispositif NEPIO, selon l’approche par jalons de l’AIEA, en marque une étape importante. Le nucléaire représente une option de long terme, complémentaire du gaz, des renouvelables, du stockage et des interconnexions ; il exige des institutions solides, une autorité de sûreté indépendante, des compétences durables et des capacités de financement adaptées. 4. Sécuriser les approvisionnements pétroliers et les chaînes logistiques. La sûreté des routes maritimes doit s’accompagner d’une diversification des fournisseurs et des itinéraires, de capacités portuaires performantes, de stocks stratégiques et de contrats d’approvisionnement robustes. Une coordination régionale des réserves et des mécanismes de solidarité en période de crise mérite d’être examinée. La contribution du secteur privé reste essentielle, dans un cadre de supervision et de régulation proportionné au caractère stratégique des produits énergétiques. 5. Faire de l’énergie un moteur d’industrialisation. La transformation locale des hydrocarbures, la pétrochimie, la fabrication d’équipements et le développement de chaînes de valeur régionales peuvent favoriser l’emploi, la compétitivité et la création de richesse. L’accès à une électricité fiable et abordable doit être considéré comme une condition de la souveraineté industrielle du continent. 6. Renforcer la diplomatie énergétique et maritime africaine. Les États africains doivent défendre le respect du droit international, en particulier de la Convention des Nations unies sur le droit de la mer. Ses articles 37 et 38 encadrent notamment le régime du passage en transit dans les détroits utilisés pour la navigation internationale. L’Union africaine et les organisations régionales pourraient davantage coordonner les positions africaines sur la liberté de navigation, la prévention des conflits, la sécurité maritime et la protection des approvisionnements essentiels. 7. Développer les infrastructures gazières et les marchés régionaux. Les gazoducs, les terminaux de GNL, les réseaux de transport de gaz et les interconnexions électriques doivent permettre de mieux valoriser les ressources africaines au bénéfice des besoins domestiques et industriels. La coopération entre le Sénégal et la Mauritanie autour du projet gazier Grand Tortue Ahmeyim (GTA) illustre le potentiel de projets transfrontaliers. Le développement gazier doit toutefois être articulé à la diversification du mix énergétique et à une trajectoire de transition maîtrisée. 8. Favoriser les partenariats industriels africains. La raffinerie du groupe Dangote, opérationnelle au Nigeria, offre un exemple d’investissement africain de grande ampleur dans la transformation pétrolière. Le projet de raffinerie envisagé au Kenya doit être distingué d’une installation déjà réalisée ; les autres intentions d’investissement doivent être mentionnées avec prudence. L’enjeu dépasse la coopération entre entreprises : il s’agit de créer des complémentarités industrielles et commerciales au service des marchés africains. 9. Mobiliser des financements et améliorer la gouvernance du secteur. La réussite de cette ambition suppose des politiques prévisibles, des régulateurs crédibles, des entreprises publiques performantes, des partenariats équilibrés et des mécanismes de financement de long terme. Les institutions africaines et les banques de développement doivent être mises davantage à contribution pour financer les infrastructures structurantes, réduire les risques et favoriser l’investissement privé. Il convient de saluer l'annonce le 31 octobre 2026 de la création de la Banque Africaine de l'Energie ( AEB) dont le siège est basé à Abuja. Portée conjointement par la Banque Africaine d'import- Export ( Afreximbank ) et l'Organisation des Producteurs de Pétrole africains ( APPO) dont le Sénégal a adhéré le 18 octobre 2022, elle est dotée d'un budget autorisé de 5 milliards de dollars US destinée à financer des projets sur l'ensemble de la chaîne de valeur énergétique, y compris l'exploration et la production des hydrocarbures, le transport et la transformation, le raffinage et la distribution. Le défi restera la mobilisation effective des ressources et de la structuration des mécanismes de financement. Les besoins en investissements dans le secteur énergétique sont estimés à 200 milliards de dollars us selon les données des institutions promotrices. 10. Investir davantage dans l'agriculture et l'industrie pour accélérer l'autosuffisance alimentaire afin de réduire fortement la dépendance sur les routes maritimes internationales. Ainsi, l'Union Africaine et les organisations d'intégration sous régionales doivent renforcer le plaidoyer pour tendre vers la souveraineté alimentaire. Conclusion : de la vulnérabilité à la souveraineté énergétique collective Les crises d’Ormuz et de Bab el-Mandeb montrent que la sécurité énergétique africaine ne peut se limiter à la disponibilité des ressources naturelles ni à la protection des importations. Elle suppose la maîtrise progressive des chaînes de valeur, la diversification des sources d’énergie, des infrastructures robustes et des institutions capables d’anticiper les crises. L’intégration régionale est, dans ce contexte, une réponse stratégique : elle peut permettre de mutualiser les investissements, d’élargir les marchés, de sécuriser les approvisionnements et d’accélérer l’accès universel à une énergie fiable et abordable. L’objectif n’est pas l’autarcie, mais une interdépendance africaine organisée, plus résiliente et plus favorable à l’industrialisation. L’Afrique ne doit plus seulement chercher à sécuriser les routes par lesquelles elle importe son énergie ; elle doit construire les infrastructures, les marchés et les solidarités qui lui permettront de mieux maîtriser son avenir énergétique. Dr Kemoko DIAKITÉ Docteur en droit public Spécialiste des questions internationales
